operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Exhausted by performance on June 17, 1957, the date the order was signed. Its only operative words revoke Executive Order No. 9775 of September 3, 1946, which established the Federal Committee on Highway Safety, a one-time act that commands nothing afterwards. The order has no effective-date wording, so it is read as effective when signed; the Federal Register issue of June 19, 1957 is the alternative reading and is disclosed here. Actor: the order itself; the end source is its own operative text. The revoked order's non-operation is the surviving consequence, not a continuing command.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10715 (22 FR 4313, PDF pages 1-1; Federal Register issue of June 19, 1957; govinfo PDF text layer held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10715.txt), headed Executive Order 10715, signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower on June 17, 1957. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Revoking Executive Order No. 9775 of September 3, 1946). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: the order has one operative sentence, the revocation of Executive Order No. 9775 of September 3, 1946, which established the Federal Committee on Highway Safety. The order states no effective date, so it took effect when signed on June 17, 1957; the Federal Register printed it on June 19, 1957, which is the alternative date a reader might take for effectiveness. The revocation is a single act that the order performs by its own words when it issues; once made it commands nothing further, so the clause is exhausted by performance on the signing date. What survives is the fact that the revoked order no longer operates, which is a consequence of the act and not a continuing command of this order. The three chosen machine searches state their coverage with no warning and their coverage notes were read. The U.S. Code and eCFR searches returned no hit for this order. The later-events search returned one hit, the Office of the Federal Register disposition note that this order revokes Executive Order 9775 and that the Federal Committee on Highway Safety is abolished; that note describes this order's own act, not a later event affecting this order (the machine status history carries the same note as a qualified-change flag, which I read and resolve the same way).

The Cruden number lookup in LOOKUPS.md (all held order texts except clause drafts) finds this number only in the held Federal Register text of this order itself. An exact-number search of the held text of EO 12553 (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_12553.txt, the 1986 mass revocation table) finds no entry for this number. No instrument earlier than June 17, 1957 is shown to have affected this order.","independent_command_check":"No command independent of the revocation: the order creates no office, delegation, fund or direction to an agency.","savings_check":"No saving wording attaches to the revocation. Its only residual is that the revoked order stays revoked; that is a completed result, not an operative command.","scope_check":"One operative clause, the revocation; it is exhausted in full by performance on June 17, 1957."}

savings_residuals.reason: The order contains no savings, exception or transitional clause; I read its whole text. The revoked order stays revoked, which is the accrued result of the act and not a command that keeps this order operative.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by its own terms at the close of Tuesday, December 31, 1957, the second of the two days on which it excuses employees for one-half day (the first is Tuesday, December 24, 1957). The order sets no later date and no continuing rule; the exclusion paragraph only limits the excusal. Recorded as 1957-12-31, inclusive; the exclusive reading (the end when December 31 begins) is the alternative. Actor: the order itself. The dossier holds no own-terms record for this order, so the end cites the order's own operative clause, which contains the stated days. No later amending event is held; Executive Order 10358 (1952) is cited by the order for its holiday definition and is earlier, not a later event.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10744 (22 FR 10001, PDF pages 1-1; Federal Register issue of December 13, 1957; govinfo PDF text layer held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10744.txt), headed Executive Order 10744, signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower on December 10, 1957. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Excusing Federal Employees From Duty for One-Half Day on December 24, and One-Half Day on December 31, 1957). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers both paragraphs of the order. The first paragraph excuses covered employees from duty for one-half day on each of two stated days, Tuesday, December 24, 1957, and Tuesday, December 31, 1957, and treats each such half-day as a holiday for the purposes of Executive Order 10358 of June 9, 1952 and of the statutes on compensation and leave, with exceptions for employees excluded by agency heads or whose absence would be inconsistent with law. The second paragraph says the order does not excuse employees whose posts of duty are required for national security or other public reasons in the judgment of their agency heads. Own terms: the last stated day is December 31, 1957, so the order's own terms end it then; I record the end inclusive at the close of that day, with the exclusive reading (the end when that day begins) as the alternative. The three chosen machine searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes plus operative sentences of 17521 saved order texts) each state their coverage with no warning; their coverage notes were read. They search by this order's number, and the one later-events hit is Executive Order 10358, an earlier order (1952) that this order itself cites for its holiday definition, so it is not a later change to this order.

The only instrument the order names is Executive Order 10358 of June 9, 1952, which predates it and supplies the holiday definition; it is not a later event. The machine-listed lead for EO 10358 (target provision not located) therefore concerns an earlier instrument and is resolved as not an end. The Cruden number lookup in LOOKUPS.md (all held order texts except clause drafts) finds this number only in the held Federal Register text of this order itself and in the held Register page text EO_10743.txt, where it is the printing of this order's own heading on a Register page shared with the neighbouring order. An exact-number search of the held text of EO 12553 (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_12553.txt, the 1986 mass revocation table) finds no entry for this number. No instrument is shown to have revoked or amended this order before December 31, 1957.","independent_command_check":"No command independent of the two stated half-days: the order creates no continuing office, delegation or rule, and its holiday treatment attaches only to those half-days.","savings_check":"No saving wording. Pay and leave granted for the two half-days are completed effects of the statutes the order invokes, not operative commands of the order.","scope_check":"One operative clause (excusal with its exceptions, plus the national-security exclusion paragraph); it ends in full on December 31, 1957, the last stated day."}

savings_residuals.reason: The order contains no savings, exception or transitional clause beyond the national-security exclusion in its second paragraph, which limits the excusal and does not continue it; I read the whole text. Pay and leave for the excused half-days rest on the compensation and leave statutes, for which the order treats each half-day as a holiday; those effects are completed and do not keep the order operative after December 31, 1957.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by its own terms at the close of Friday, December 26, 1958, the only day the order names, on which it excuses covered employees from duty all day. The leave-policy paragraph refers to the holiday period without dates, so it adds no later stated day; it is read as tied to the excused day. Recorded as 1958-12-26, inclusive. Alternatives disclosed: the exclusive reading (the end when December 26 begins) and a broader reading under which the leave direction would extend through the unspecified holiday period. Actor: the order itself. The dossier holds no own-terms record, so the end cites the order's own clause, which contains the stated day. No later amending event is held.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10792 (23 FR 9307, PDF pages 1-1; Federal Register issue of December 3, 1958; govinfo PDF text layer held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10792.txt), headed Executive Order 10792, signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower on November 28, 1958. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Excusing Federal Employees From Duty All Day on December 26, 1958). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers all three paragraphs. The first excuses covered employees from duty all day on Friday, December 26, 1958, the day after Christmas, and treats that day as a holiday for the purposes of Executive Order 10358 of June 9, 1952 and of the statutes on compensation and leave, with exceptions for employees excluded by agency heads or whose absence would be inconsistent with law. The second directs agency heads, to the extent consistent with the needs of the service, to adopt a liberal policy for annual leave for employees who wish to take leave over the holiday period; it states no dates. The third says the order does not excuse employees whose posts of duty are required for national security or other public reasons. Own terms: the only stated day is December 26, 1958. The leave direction speaks of the holiday period without defining it, so no held text fixes a later end for it; I treat it as tied to the excused day and record the end at the close of December 26, 1958, inclusive, and disclose two alternatives: the exclusive reading (end when that day begins) and a broader reading under which the leave direction would run to the end of the Christmas and New Year period, which the order does not date. The three chosen machine searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes plus operative sentences of 17521 saved order texts) each state their coverage with no warning; their coverage notes were read. They search by this order's number, and none returned a hit for it.

The Cruden number lookup in LOOKUPS.md (all held order texts except clause drafts) finds this number only in the held Federal Register text of this order itself and in the held Register page text EO_10791.txt, where it is the printing of this order's own heading on a Register page shared with the neighbouring order. An exact-number search of the held text of EO 12553 (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_12553.txt, the 1986 mass revocation table) finds no entry for this number. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by its own terms at the end of the Eighty-sixth Congress. Executive Order 10806, signed March 10, 1959 (24 FR 1823, PDF pages 1-1), orders that income, excess-profits, estate and gift tax (years 1947 to 1959, inclusive) returns shall, during the Eighty-sixth Congress, be open to inspection by the Senate Committee on Government Operations, or any duly authorized subcommittee, in connection with its studies of the operation of Government activities at all levels with a view to determining the economy and efficiency of the Government. The order sets no other term, condition or revocation clause. The terms of the Members of the Eighty-sixth Congress ended at noon on January 3, 1961 under the Twentieth Amendment, so the grant lapsed no later than that day; recorded as 1961-01-03 inclusive, with the exclusive reading (end when that day begins) disclosed as the alternative. The end source is the order's own operative text. No later amending event is held.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10806 (24 FR 1823, PDF pages 1-1; Federal Register issue of March 13, 1959; govinfo PDF text layer held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10806.txt), headed Executive Order 10806, signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower on March 10, 1959. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Inspection of Income, Excess-Profits, Estate, and Gift Tax Returns by the Senate Committee on Government Operations). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: the order is one grant, a single sentence opening income, excess-profits, estate and gift tax (years 1947 to 1959, inclusive) returns to inspection by the Senate Committee on Government Operations or any duly authorized subcommittee, followed by a sentence fixing its effective date on filing for publication. The grant is limited by its own words to the period of the Eighty-sixth Congress, which I treat as the order's fixed term. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Inspection of Income, Excess-Profits, Declared-Value Excess-Profits, Capital-Stock, Estate, and Gift Tax Returns by the Senate Committee on the Judiciary). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: the order is one grant, a single sentence opening income, excess-profits, declared-value excess-profits, capital-stock, estate and gift tax (years 1945 to 1958, inclusive) returns to inspection by the Senate Committee on the Judiciary or any duly authorized subcommittee, followed by a sentence fixing its effective date on filing for publication. The grant is limited by its own words to the period of the Eighty-sixth Congress, which I treat as the order's fixed term. The terms of the Members of the Eighty-sixth Congress began at noon on January 3, 1959 and ended at noon on January 3, 1961 (Twentieth Amendment, sections 1 and 2). The Constitution is not among the held texts and no held source states that date, so the end date rests on that constitutional text together with the order's own words; no other source is claimed for it. First end: January 3, 1961 by the order's own terms, recorded inclusive. The exclusive reading (the end when that day begins) is the alternative the owner ruling requires me to disclose, but it fits poorly here because the Congress's terms ran until noon of that day. The three chosen machine searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes plus operative sentences of 17521 saved order texts) each state their coverage with no warning; their coverage notes were read. They search by this order's number, and none returned a hit for it.

PART 914— N A V EL ORANGES

Limitation of Handling 
§ 914.462 Navel Orange Regulation 162.
(a) Findings.  (1) Pursuant to the 
marketing agreement, as amended, and 
Order No. 14, as amended (7 CFR Part 
914), regulating the handling of navel 
oranges grown in Arizona and designated 
part of California, effective under the 
applicable provisions of the Agricultural 
Marketing Agreement Act of 1937, as 
amended (7 U.S.C. 601 et seq.; 68 Stat. 
906, 1047), and upon the basis of the 
recommendation and information sub­
mitted by the Navel Orange Administra­
tive Committee, established under the 
said amended marketing agreement and 
order, and upon other available infor­
mation, it is hereby found that the limi­
tation of handling of such navel oranges 
as hereinafter provided will tend to ef­
fectuate the declared policy of the act.
(2) It is hereby further found that it is 
impracticable and contrary to the public 
interest to give preliminary notice, en­
gage in public rule-making procedure, 
and postpone the effective date of this 
section until 3Ü  days after publication 
hereof in the F ederal R egister  (60 Stat. 
237; 5 U.S.C. 1001 et seq.) because the 
time intervening between the date when 
information upon which this section is 
based became available and the time 
when this section must become effective 
in order to effectuate the declared policy 
of the act is insufficient, and a reason­
able time is permitted, under the cir­
cumstances, for preparation for such 
effective time; and good cause exists for 
making the provisions hereof effective as 
hereinafter set forth. The committee 
held an open meeting during the current 
week, after giving due notice thereof, to 
consider supply and market conditions^ 
for navel oranges and the need for reg­
ulation; interested persons were afforded 
an opportunity to submit information 
and views at this meeting; the recom­
mendation and supporting information 
for regulation during the period speci­
fied herein were promptly submitted to 
the Department after such meeting was 
held; the provisions of this section, in­
cluding its effective time, are identical 
with the aforesaid recommendation of 
the committee, and information con­
cerning such provisions and effective 
time has been disseminated among han­
dlers of such navel oranges; it is neces­
sary, in order to effectuate the declared 
policy of the act, to make this section 
effective during the period herein speci­
fied; and compliance with this section 
will not require any special preparation 
on the part of persons subject hereto
which cannot be completed on or before 
the effective date hereof . Such commit­
tee meeting was held on March 19, 1959.
(b) ■  Order.  (1) The respective quan­
tities of navel oranges grown in Arizona 
and designated part of California which 
may be handled during the period be­
ginning at 12:01 a.m., P.s.t., March 22, 
1959, and ending at 12:01 a.m., P.s.t., 
March 29, 1959, are hereby fixed as 
follows:
(1) District 1: 554,400 cartons;
(ii) District 2: 739,200 cartons;
(iii) District 3: Unlimited movement;
(iv) District 4: Unlimited movement.
(2) All navel oranges handled during 
the period specified in this section are 
subject also to all applicable size restric­
tions which are in effect pursuant to this 
part during such period.
(3) As used in this section, “handled,” 
“District 1,” “District 2,” “District 3,” 
“District 4,” and “carton” have the same 
meaning as when used in said amended

PART 953— LEMONS GROWN IN  
CALIFORNIA AND ARIZONA
Limitation of Handling 
§ 953.891 ' Lemon Regulation 784.
(a) Findings.  (1) Pursuant to the 
marketing agreement, as amended, and 
Order No. 53, as amended (7 CFR Part 
953; 23 F.R. 9053), regulating the han­
dling of lemons grown in California and 
Arizoná, effective under the applicable 
provisions of the Agricultural Marketing 
Agreement Act of 1937, as amended (7 
U.S.C. 601 et seq.; 68 Stat. 906, 1047), 
and upon the basis of the recommenda­
tion and information submitted by the 
Lemon Administrative Committee, estab­
lished under the said amended marketing 
agreement and order, and upon other 
available information, it is hereby found 
that the limitation of handling of such 
lemons as hereinafter provided will tend 
to effectuate the declared policy of the 
act.
(2) It is hereby further found thát it 
is impracticable and contrary to the pub­
lic interest tp give preliminary notice, 
engage in public rule-making procedure, 
and postpone the effective date of this 
section until 30 days after publication 
hereof in the F ederal  R egister  (60 Stat. 
237; 5 U.S.C. 1001 et seq.) because the 
time intervening between the date when 
information upon which this section is 
based becomes available and the time 
when this section must become effective
in order to effectuate the declared policy 
of the act is insufficient, and a reasonable 
time is permitted, under the circum­
stances, for preparation for such effective 
time; and good cause exists for making 
the provisions hereof effective as herein­
after set forth. The Committee held an 
open meeting during the current w eek, 
after giving due notice thereof, to con­
sider supply and market conditions for 
lemons and the need for regulation; in­
terested persons were afforded an oppor­
tunity to submit information and view s 
at this meeting; the recommendation 
and supporting information for regula­
tion during the period specified herein 
were promptly submitted to the Depart­
ment after such meeting was held; the 
provisions of this section, including its 
effective time, are identical with the 
aforesaid recommendation of the com­
mittee, and information concerning 
such provisions and effective time has 
been disseminated among handlers of 
such lemons; it is necessary, in order to 
effectuate the declared policy of the act, 
to make this section effective during the 
period herein specified; and compliance 
with this section will not require any spe­
cial preparation on the part of persons 
subject heretd which cannot be com­
pleted on or before the effective date 
hereof. Such committee meeting w as 
held on March 18,1959.
<b) Order.  (1) The respective quan­
tities of lemons grown in California and 
Arizona which may be handled during 
the period begining at 12:01 a.m., P.s.t., 
March 22,1959, and ending at 12:01 a.m., 
P.s.t., March 29,1959, are hereby fixed as 
follows:
(1) District 1: 13,020 cartons;
(ii) District 2: 196,230 cartons;
(iii) District 3: Unlimited movement.
(2) As used in this section, “handled, 
“District 1,” “District 2,” “District 3,’ and 
“carton” have the same meaning as when 
used in the said amended marketing 
agreement and order.

608c)

Executive O rder 10814
INSPECTION OF STATISTICAL TRAN­
SCRIPT CARDS AND CORPORATION 
AND INDIVIDUAL INCOME TAX  
RETURNS BY THE SECURITIES AND  
EXCHANGE COMMISSION
By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by section 55(a) of the Internal Revenue  
Code of 1939 (53 Stat. 29; 54 Stat.  
1008; 55 Stat. 722; 26 U.S.C. 55(a)) and  
by section 6103(a) of the Internal  
Revenue Code of 1954 (68A Stat. 753; 26  
U.S.C. 6103(a)), and in the interest of  
the internal management of the Govern­
ment, it is hereby ordered that statistical  
transcript cards prepared by the Internal  
Revenue Service from income tax re­
turns of corporations made for taxable  
years ending after December 31, 1952,  
and corporate and individual income tax  
returns made for taxable years ending  
after December 31, 1956, shall be open  
to inspection by the Securities and Ex­
change Commission as may be needed  
in gathering statistical information in  
carrying out its functions under the  
Securities Exchange Act of 1934, ap­
proved June 6, 1934 (48 Stat. 881; 1 5  
U.S.C. 78a-78jj), as amended, or in  
complying with directives or recom­
mendations of the Bureau of the Budget  
pursuant to section 103 of the Budget  
and Accounting Procedures Act of 1 9 5 0 , 
approved September 12, 1950 (64 Stat.  
834 ; 31 U.S.C. 18b), relating to the devel­
opment of programs for preparing  
statistical information by Executive  
agencies. Such inspection shall be in  
accordance and upon compliance with  
the rules and regulations prescribed by  
the Secretary of the Treasury in the two 
Treasury decisions,1  relating to the in­
spection of certain „transcript cards and 
income tax returns by the Securities and 
Exchange Commission, approved by m e 
this date.
This order shall be effective upon its  
filing for publication in the Federal 
R egister .
D w ig h t D. E isenhower
T he  W hite  H ouse ,
April 29, 1959.

Executive O rder 10815

PROFITS, ESTATE, AND GIFT TAX  
RETURNS BY THE COMMITTEE O N 
UN-AMERICAN ACTIVITIES, HOUSE 
OF REPRESENTATIVES
By virtue of the authority vested in m e 
by sections 55(a), 508, and 729(a) of the  
Internal Revenue Code of 1939 (53 Stat. 
29, 111; 54 Stat. 989,’ 1008; 26 U.S.C. 5 5
(a ), 508, and 729(a)), and by section  
6103(a) of the Internal Revenue Code of  
1954 (68A Stat. 753; 26 U.S.C. 6103(a)),  
it is hereby ordered that any income,  
excess-profits, estate, or gift tax return  
for the years 1945 to 1959, inclusive,  
shall, during the Eighty-sixth Congress,  
be open to inspection by the Committee 
on Un-American Activities, House of  
Representatives, or any duly authorized  
subcommittee thereof, for the purpose of 
carrying on those investigations author­
ized by clause XI of Rule XI of the Rules 
of the House of Representatives, agreed  
to January 7, 1959, such inspection to be 
in accordance and upon compliance with 
the rules and regulations prescribed by  
the Secretary of the Treasury in Treas­
ury Decisions 6132 and 6133, relating to 
the inspection of returns by committees 
of the Congress, approved by me on May 
3 1955.
This order shall be effective upon its  
filing for publication in the Federal 
R egister .
D w ight D. Eisenhower

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by its own terms at the end of the Eighty-sixth Congress. Executive Order 10815, signed April 29, 1959 (24 FR 3474, PDF pages 10-10), orders that income, excess-profits, estate and gift tax (years 1945 to 1959, inclusive) returns shall, during the Eighty-sixth Congress, be open to inspection by the Committee on Un-American Activities, House of Representatives, or any duly authorized subcommittee, for the purpose of carrying on the investigations authorized by the House rule agreed to January 7, 1959. The order sets no other term, condition or revocation clause. The terms of the Members of the Eighty-sixth Congress ended at noon on January 3, 1961 under the Twentieth Amendment, so the grant lapsed no later than that day; recorded as 1961-01-03 inclusive, with the exclusive reading (end when that day begins) disclosed as the alternative. The end source is the order's own operative text. No later amending event is held.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10815 (24 FR 3474, PDF pages 10-10; Federal Register issue of May 1, 1959; govinfo PDF text layer held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10815.txt), headed Executive Order 10815, signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower on April 29, 1959. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Inspection of Income, Excess-Profits, Estate, and Gift Tax Returns by the Committee on Un-American Activities, House of Representatives). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: the order is one grant, a single sentence opening income, excess-profits, estate and gift tax (years 1945 to 1959, inclusive) returns to inspection by the Committee on Un-American Activities, House of Representatives or any duly authorized subcommittee, followed by a sentence fixing its effective date on filing for publication. The dossier clauses for this number belong to another document, so the inventory is corrected (see inventory reason). The grant is limited by its own words to the period of the Eighty-sixth Congress, which I treat as the order's fixed term. The terms of the Members of the Eighty-sixth Congress began at noon on January 3, 1959 and ended at noon on January 3, 1961 (Twentieth Amendment, sections 1 and 2). The Constitution is not among the held texts and no held source states that date, so the end date rests on that constitutional text together with the order's own words; no other source is claimed for it. First end: January 3, 1961 by the order's own terms, recorded inclusive. The exclusive reading (the end when that day begins) is the alternative the owner ruling requires me to disclose, but it fits poorly here because the Congress's terms ran until noon of that day. The three chosen machine searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes plus operative sentences of 17521 saved order texts) each state their coverage with no warning; their coverage notes were read. They search by this order's number, and none returned a hit for it.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The purpose the order states (House rule agreed to January 7, 1959) explains why the committee may inspect and is not a limit on the grant's term; no held text shows that purpose withdrawn or exhausted before the Congress ended. (2) The recital of Treasury Decisions 6132 and 6133 governs how inspection proceeds and sets no end. (3) The effective-date sentence starts the grant and is not an end. (4) The Cruden number lookup in LOOKUPS.md (all held order texts except clause drafts) finds no held text that cites this number; the order's own heading is spaced out by OCR in the held text and is not matched, so the lookup shows no other text naming it. An exact-number search of the held text of EO 12553 (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_12553.txt, the 1986 mass revocation table) finds no entry for this number. No other instrument is shown to have revoked, superseded or terminated the grant before January 3, 1961.","independent_command_check":"The order commands nothing independent of the inspection grant: the Treasury Decisions recital sets the manner of inspection and the effective-date sentence is not a command. No appointment, delegation or direction to an agency survives the grant.","savings_check":"The order has no saving wording. Inspections already made are completed acts that rest on the grant and do not keep it operative after January 3, 1961.","scope_check":"The order has one operative clause and it ends in full on January 3, 1961. The dossier clause was misplaced, so the inventory is corrected as stated in the inventory reason."}

savings_residuals.reason: The order contains no savings, exception or transitional clause; I read its whole text for such wording. Any inspection made while the grant ran is a completed act, and nothing in the order continues the grant after the Eighty-sixth Congress ended. Any later statutory change to the Internal Revenue Code sections the order cites would postdate this end and cannot be a first end.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by its own terms at the end of the Eighty-sixth Congress. Executive Order 10818, signed May 8, 1959 (24 FR 3779, PDF pages 3-3), orders that income, excess-profits, estate and gift tax (years 1945 to 1959, inclusive) returns shall, during the Eighty-sixth Congress, be open to inspection by the Committee on Government Operations, House of Representatives, or any duly authorized subcommittee, in connection with its studies of the operation of Government activities at all levels with a view to determining the economy and efficiency of the Government. The order sets no other term, condition or revocation clause. The terms of the Members of the Eighty-sixth Congress ended at noon on January 3, 1961 under the Twentieth Amendment, so the grant lapsed no later than that day; recorded as 1961-01-03 inclusive, with the exclusive reading (end when that day begins) disclosed as the alternative. The end source is the order's own operative text. No later amending event is held.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10818 (24 FR 3779, PDF pages 3-3; Federal Register issue of May 12, 1959; govinfo PDF text layer held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10818.txt), headed Executive Order 10818, signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower on May 8, 1959. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Inspection of Income, Excess-Profits, Estate, and Gift Tax Returns by the Committee on Government Operations, House of Representatives). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: the order is one grant, a single sentence opening income, excess-profits, estate and gift tax (years 1945 to 1959, inclusive) returns to inspection by the Committee on Government Operations, House of Representatives or any duly authorized subcommittee, followed by a sentence fixing its effective date on filing for publication. The grant is limited by its own words to the period of the Eighty-sixth Congress, which I treat as the order's fixed term. The terms of the Members of the Eighty-sixth Congress began at noon on January 3, 1959 and ended at noon on January 3, 1961 (Twentieth Amendment, sections 1 and 2). The Constitution is not among the held texts and no held source states that date, so the end date rests on that constitutional text together with the order's own words; no other source is claimed for it. First end: January 3, 1961 by the order's own terms, recorded inclusive. The exclusive reading (the end when that day begins) is the alternative the owner ruling requires me to disclose, but it fits poorly here because the Congress's terms ran until noon of that day. The dossier's lead naming Executive Order 10819 (cited by number, no change provision located) is resolved by reading the held text of EO 10819: it is a separate order amending section 301 of Executive Order 10480 on the defense mobilization program, printed on the same Register page as this order, and it neither names nor affects this order. The three chosen machine searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes plus operative sentences of 17521 saved order texts) each state their coverage with no warning; their coverage notes were read. They search by this order's number, and none returned a hit for it.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The purpose the order states (its studies of Government operations) explains why the committee may inspect and is not a limit on the grant's term; no held text shows that purpose withdrawn or exhausted before the Congress ended. (2) The recital of Treasury Decisions 6132 and 6133 governs how inspection proceeds and sets no end. (3) The effective-date sentence starts the grant and is not an end. (4) The Cruden number lookup in LOOKUPS.md (all held order texts except clause drafts) finds this number only in the held Federal Register text of this order itself and in the held Register page texts EO_10817.txt, EO_10819.txt, where it is the printing of this order's own heading on a Register page shared with the neighbouring order. An exact-number search of the held text of EO 12553 (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_12553.txt, the 1986 mass revocation table) finds no entry for this number. No other instrument is shown to have revoked, superseded or terminated the grant before January 3, 1961.","independent_command_check":"The order commands nothing independent of the inspection grant: the Treasury Decisions recital sets the manner of inspection and the effective-date sentence is not a command. No appointment, delegation or direction to an agency survives the grant.","savings_check":"The order has no saving wording. Inspections already made are completed acts that rest on the grant and do not keep it operative after January 3, 1961.","scope_check":"The order has one operative clause and it ends in full on January 3, 1961. The dossier inventory (one whole-order clause) is complete."}

savings_residuals.reason: The order contains no savings, exception or transitional clause; I read its whole text for such wording. Any inspection made while the grant ran is a completed act, and nothing in the order continues the grant after the Eighty-sixth Congress ended. Any later statutory change to the Internal Revenue Code sections the order cites would postdate this end and cannot be a first end.

By virtue of the authority vested in me  
by sections 55(a), 508, and 729(a) of the  
Internal Revenue Code of 1939 (53 Stat.

ury in Treasury Decisions 6132 and 6133,

Executive O rdlr 10819
AMENDMENT OF EXECUTIVE ORDER  
NO. 10480,1  AS AMENDED, RELAT­
ING TO THE DEFENSE MOBILIZA­
TION PROGRAM
By virtue of the authority vested in  
me by the Constitution and laws of the  
United States, including the Defense  
Production Act of 1950, as amended (50  
U.S.C. App. 2061 et  sea.), and as Presi­
dent of the United States, it is ordered  
that Executive Order No. 10480 of Au­
gust 14, 1953, entitled “Further Provid­
ing for the Administration of the Defense  
Mobilization Program,” as amended, be,  
and it is hereby, further amended by  
substituting for section 301 thereof, as  
amended by Executive Order No. 10574  
of November 5, 1954, a new section 301  
reading as follows:
“S ec. 301. The Department of the  
Army, the Department of the Navy, the  
Department of the Air Force, the Atomic  
Energy Commission, the Department of  
Commerce, the Department of the Inte­
rior, the Department of Agriculture, the  
General Services Administration, and  
the National Aeronautics and Space Ad­
ministration, in this Part referred to as  
guaranteeing agencies, each officer hav­
ing functions delegated to him pursuant  
to section 201 (à) of this order, and each  
other agency of the Government having  
mobilization functions, shall, within  
areas of production designated by the  
Director of the Office of Civil and De­
fense Mobilization, develop and promote  
measures for the expansion of produc­
tive capacity and of production and sup­
ply of materials and facilities necessary  
for the national defense.”

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10825 (24 FR 4825, PDF pages 1-3; Federal Register issue of June 13, 1959; govinfo PDF text layer held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10825.txt), headed Executive Order 10825, signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower on June 12, 1959. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Excusing Federal Employees From Duty All Day on July 3, 1959). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: section 1(a) excuses covered employees from duty all day on Friday, July 3, 1959 (with section 1(b) giving a rule for employees whose workday spans two calendar days); section 2 limits the excusal for national-security employees and employees working or excused on Saturday, July 4, 1959; section 3 gives employees who are not excused on July 3, 1959 one other workday off in fiscal year 1960; section 4 denies any basis for holiday, premium or overtime pay for July 3, 1959 and requests agency heads to arrange their affairs for the excusal. Inventory correction: the dossier's second clause (subsection (b)) runs from section 1 across a Register page break and then through the Contents and unrelated Register documents. The order is split by a page break (continued on next page), and the last sentence of section 4 is badly damaged in the text layer; I use five spans: section 1, section 2, section 3, the first part of section 4, and the surviving fragment of the end of section 4. The recitals are not operative and are not clauses. The damaged fragment is read against the American Presidency Project transcription (not quoted, and not cited as a source), which shows that the last sentence of section 4 requests agency heads to arrange their affairs so that employees can be excused from duty on that day or given compensatory time, without additional appropriations. Own terms: sections 1, 2 and 4 are tied to July 3 and 4, 1959; section 3 runs to the end of fiscal year 1960, which is June 30, 1960 (the Government's fiscal year ran from July 1 to June 30; that statutory definition is not a held text and the order does not state the date, so I disclose that the end of section 3 rests on it). The whole order therefore ends on June 30, 1960. The three chosen machine searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes plus operative sentences of 17521 saved order texts) each state their coverage with no warning; their coverage notes were read. They search by this order's number, and none returned a hit for it.

An exact-number search of the held text of EO 12553 (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_12553.txt, the 1986 mass revocation table) finds no entry for this number. No instrument is shown to have revoked or amended this order, or to have cancelled the section 3 alternate workday, before the dates given.","independent_command_check":"Section 3 is the one command that outlasts the July 3 excusal, and it has its own end (fiscal year 1960); no other command is independent of the excused day.","savings_check":"No saving wording. savings_residuals.reason: The order contains no savings, exception or transitional clause beyond the limits in section 2 and the pay denial in section 4, which restrict the excusal and do not continue it. Pay and leave for the excused day and for the alternate workday rest on the leave statutes and are completed effects.

NUMBER 163
Title 3— THE PRESIDENT
Executive Order 10832
REVOCATION OF EXECUTIVE ORDER  
NO. 9887,1  DESIGNATING CERTAIN 
PUBLIC INTERNATIONAL ORGANI­
ZATIONS ENTITLED TO ENJOY  
CERTAIN PRIVILEGES, EXEMP­
TIONS, AND IMMUNITIES
WHEREAS Executive Order No. 9887 
of August 22, 1947, designated the Pre­
paratory Commission for the Interna­
tional Refugee Organization and its 
successor, the International Refugee 
Organization, as public international 
organizations entitled to enjoy the 
privileges, exemptions, and immunities 
conferred by the International Organi­
zations Immunities Act, approved De­
cember 29, 1945 (22 U.S.C. 288) ; and 
WHEREAS those organizations have ceased to exist:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 1  of 
International Organizations Im­
munities Act, it is ordered that Execu­
tive Order No. 9887 of August 22, 1947, 
be, and it is hereby, revoked.
D wight  D. E isenhower  
The White  H ouse,
August 18, 1Q 59.

Title 7— AGRICULTURE
Chapter IX— Agricultural.  Marketing 
Service (Marketing Agreements and 
Orders), Department of Agriculture
[Milk Order No. 119]
PART 1019— MILK IN CONNECTICUT  
MARKETING AREA  
Order Terminating Certain Provisions  
Pursuant to the provisions of the Agri- 
5JS Marketing Agreement Act of 
*»¿7, as amended (7 U.S.C. 601 et seq.),
P.664 PR ' 5723' 8 CPR*  1943— 1948 Comp.,
and of the order regulating the handling 
of milk in the Connecticut marketing 
area (7 CFR Part 1019), it is hereby 
found and determined that:
(a) The following provision of the or­
der, no longer tends to effectuate the de­
clared policy of the Act:
(1) The provision “period between the 
15th day of the month for which the 
price is computed and the 16th day of the 
preceding” and including the word “in­
clusive” as it appears in §  1019.40(b) (1) 
of the order.
The Class II price under the Connecti­
cut order was intended to be established 
on the same basis as that used in the 
pricing of Class n  milk under the Boston, 
Massachusetts, order as stated in the 
final decision on the Connecticut Class II 
price (24 F.R. 1049, Part ID dated Febru­
ary 11, 1959. The decision specifically 
point out that “The formula herein 
adopted would base the- butterfat value 
of Class II milk on the Boston market 
quotations per 40-quart can of 40 percent 
bottling quality cream, as reported for 
the month by the United States Depart­
ment of Agriculture”.
The aforesaid provision proposed for 
termination was inadvertently Included 
in the order language through error and 
should be terminated to conform to the 
intent of the decision.
During the period from the inception 
of the order, effective March 1, 1959 to 
the present time an alternative Class n  
price formula provided in the order 
which is based on the price of mill? for 
manufacturing purposes has been used in 
the absence of a cream price to establish 
the Class n  price. Recently, supplies of 
cream from producer receipts have de­
clined to the extent that substantial 
quantities of outside cream have been re­
ceived on the market. It appears likely 
that sufficient cream has been received to 
establish a weighted average cream price 
for the first month since the order be­
came effective. Therefore, to prevent an 
inappropriate Class II price under the 
Connecticut order in relation to the Class 
II price in the other New England orders 
due to use of a different base period for 
quotations, the aforesaid provision 
should be terminated.
(Continued on p. 6755)

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Exhausted by performance on August 18, 1959, the date the order was signed. Its only operative words revoke Executive Order No. 9887 of August 22, 1947, which designated the Preparatory Commission for the International Refugee Organization and its successor as public international organizations under the International Organizations Immunities Act, a one-time act that commands nothing afterwards. The order has no effective-date wording, so it is read as effective when signed; the Federal Register issue of August 20, 1959 is the alternative reading and is disclosed here. Actor: the order itself; the end source is its own operative text. The revoked order's non-operation is the surviving consequence, not a continuing command.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10832 (24 FR 6753, PDF pages 1-1; Federal Register issue of August 20, 1959; govinfo PDF text layer held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10832.txt), headed Executive Order 10832, signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower on August 18, 1959. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Revocation of EO 9887, Designating Certain  Public International Organizations Entitled To Enjoy Certain Privileges,  Exemptions, and Immunities). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: the order has one operative sentence, the revocation of Executive Order No. 9887 of August 22, 1947, which designated the Preparatory Commission for the International Refugee Organization and its successor as public international organizations under the International Organizations Immunities Act. The order also has two recitals, one stating what Executive Order 9887 did and one stating that those organizations have ceased to exist, and an enacting clause citing section 1 of the International Organizations Immunities Act; neither recital is a separate command. The order states no effective date, so it took effect when signed on August 18, 1959; the Federal Register printed it on August 20, 1959, which is the alternative date a reader might take for effectiveness. The revocation is a single act that the order performs by its own words when it issues; once made it commands nothing further, so the clause is exhausted by performance on the signing date. What survives is the fact that the revoked order no longer operates, which is a consequence of the act and not a continuing command of this order. The three chosen machine searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes plus operative sentences of 17521 saved order texts) each state their coverage with no warning; their coverage notes were read. They search by this order's number, and none returned a hit for it.

An exact-number search of the held text of EO 12553 (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_12553.txt, the 1986 mass revocation table) finds no entry for this number. No instrument earlier than August 18, 1959 is shown to have affected this order.","independent_command_check":"No command independent of the revocation: the order creates no office, delegation, fund or direction to an agency.","savings_check":"No saving wording attaches to the revocation. research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10846 (24 FR 8318, PDF pages 2-3; Federal Register issue of October 14, 1959; govinfo PDF text layer held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10846.txt), headed Executive Order 10846, signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower on October 12, 1959. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Inspection of Income, Excess-Profits, Estate, and Gift Tax Returns by the Senate Committee on Agriculture and Forestry). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: the order is one grant, a single sentence opening income, excess-profits, estate and gift tax (years 1950 to 1959, inclusive) returns to inspection by the Senate Committee on Agriculture and Forestry or any duly authorized subcommittee, followed by a sentence fixing its effective date on filing for publication. The grant is limited by its own words to the period of the Eighty-sixth Congress, which I treat as the order's fixed term. The terms of the Members of the Eighty-sixth Congress began at noon on January 3, 1959 and ended at noon on January 3, 1961 (Twentieth Amendment, sections 1 and 2). The Constitution is not among the held texts and no held source states that date, so the end date rests on that constitutional text together with the order's own words; no other source is claimed for it. First end: January 3, 1961 by the order's own terms, recorded inclusive. The exclusive reading (the end when that day begins) is the alternative the owner ruling requires me to disclose, but it fits poorly here because the Congress's terms ran until noon of that day. The three chosen machine searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes plus operative sentences of 17521 saved order texts) each state their coverage with no warning; their coverage notes were read. They search by this order's number, and none returned a hit for it.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The purpose the order states (committee resolution agreed to May 20, 1959) explains why the committee may inspect and is not a limit on the grant's term; no held text shows that purpose withdrawn or exhausted before the Congress ended. (2) The recital of Treasury Decisions 6132 and 6133 governs how inspection proceeds and sets no end. (3) The effective-date sentence starts the grant and is not an end. (4) The Cruden number lookup in LOOKUPS.md (all held order texts except clause drafts) finds this number only in the held Federal Register text of this order itself and in the held Register page text EO_10845.txt, where it is the printing of this order's own heading on a Register page shared with the neighbouring order. An exact-number search of the held text of EO 12553 (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_12553.txt, the 1986 mass revocation table) finds no entry for this number. No other instrument is shown to have revoked, superseded or terminated the grant before January 3, 1961.","independent_command_check":"The order commands nothing independent of the inspection grant: the Treasury Decisions recital sets the manner of inspection and the effective-date sentence is not a command. No appointment, delegation or direction to an agency survives the grant.","savings_check":"The order has no saving wording. Inspections already made are completed acts that rest on the grant and do not keep it operative after January 3, 1961.","scope_check":"The order has one operative clause and it ends in full on January 3, 1961. The dossier inventory (one whole-order clause) is complete."}

savings_residuals.reason: The order contains no savings, exception or transitional clause; I read its whole text for such wording. Any inspection made while the grant ran is a completed act, and nothing in the order continues the grant after the Eighty-sixth Congress ended. Any later statutory change to the Internal Revenue Code sections the order cites would postdate this end and cannot be a first end.

Executive Order 10847

RURAL DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM
WHEREAS a substantial number of 
families, both farm and non-farm, living 
in rural areas have relatively low cash 
incomes and do not share equitably in 
the economic and social progress of the 
Nation, and it is desirable to encourage 
and assist such families by providing 
greater opportunity for their participa­
tion in the Nation’s production t>f goods 
and services and in comfhunity, civic*, 
and other affairs; and 
WHEREAS the Federal Government, 
in cooperation with the several States 
i — and local governments and private agen­
cies and individuals, has undertaken a 
rural-development program designed to 
i  develop the human resources in rural 
America by a series of concerted actions 
s  to identify the needs of low-income rural 
people and to help them to achieve 
greater rewards for their contributions 
to our national progress; and 
WHEREAS the rural-development 
program has achieved steady progress to­
ward its objectives, and the time has now 
come to consolidate its accomplishments 
and to provide more formal Federal Or­
ganization jf or the program:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me as President of
FEDERAL REGISTER
the United States, it is hereby ordered as 
follows :
S e ctio n-1. (a ) There is hereby estab­
lished the Committee for Rural Develop­
ment Program, hereinafter referred to 
as the Committee, which shall be com­
posed of the following members;
(1) The Under Secretary of Agricul­
ture, who shall be the Chairman of the 
Committee.
(2) The Under Secretary of the 
Interior.
(3) The Under Secretary of Com­
merce.
(4) Th¿Under Secretary of Labor.
(5) The Under Secretary of Health, 
Education, and Welfare.
- (6) The Administrator of the Small 
Business Administration.
(7) A member of the Council of Eco­
nomic Advisers designated by the Chair- 
ÿ man of the Coüncil.
(b) To assure effective functioning of 
the Committee and uninterrupted par­
ticipation of each department and 
agency represented on the Committee, 
the head of each such department or 
agency shall designate an appropriate 
officer or employee of his department or 
agency as an alternate member to par­
ticipate in the affairs of the Committee 
whenever the member may be absent dr 
otherwise unable to participate.
(c) The Committee may request the 
head of any other Federal department 
or agency to designate a representative 
to participate in the affairs of the Com­
mittee as desirable in furthering the 
work of the rural-development program 
and related activities.
Sec. 2. The activities of the Commit­
tee shall be directed toward providing 
leadership and uniform policy guidance 
to the several Federal departments and 
agencies responsible for rural-develop­
ment program functions and related
8319
activities so that they may take more 
effective and concerted actions in carry­
ing out those functions and activities and 
cooperate more effectively with ' non- 
Federal participants, both private and 
governmental, in the program.
Sec. 3. In conducting its activities, the 
Committee shall place particular em­
phasis on effective public and private co­
operation and leadership for rural 
development at the State and local levels, 
and, to that end, shall provide guidance 
for the conduct of Federal rural-develop­
ment program functions and related 
activities in a manner designed to pro­
duce maximum State, local, and private 
participation and initiative in-identify­
ing and meeting local needs.
Sec. 4. Each department and agency 
responsible for functions and activities 
that can contribute to the objectives of 
the rural-development program and re­
lated activities shall Carry those func­
tions and activities forward in such a 
manner as to make the fullest possible 
contribution to the objectives of rural 
development.
Sec. 5. The departments and agencies 
represented on the Committee shall, as 
may be necessary for the purpose of ef­
fectuating the provisions of this order, 
furnish assistance to the Committee in 
consonance with section 214 of the act of 
May 3, 1945, 59 Stat. 134 (31 U.S.C. 691). 
Such assistance may include the detail­
ing of employees to the Committee, one 
of whom may serve as its executive secre­
tary, to perform such functions con­
sistent with the purpose of this order 
as the Committee may assign !to them.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by its own terms at the end of the Eighty-sixth Congress. Executive Order 10855, signed November 27, 1959 (24 FR 9565, PDF pages 7-7), orders that income tax (years 1945 to 1958, inclusive, as the order first read; Executive Order 10876 later changed the closing year to 1959) returns shall, during the Eighty-sixth Congress, be open to inspection by the Senate Committee on the Judiciary, or any duly authorized subcommittee, in connection with its study and investigation of the applicability of the antitrust and anti-monopoly laws of the United States to professional boxing, pursuant to Senate Resolution 57, 86th Congress, agreed to February 2, 1959. The order sets no other term, condition or revocation clause. The terms of the Members of the Eighty-sixth Congress ended at noon on January 3, 1961 under the Twentieth Amendment, so the grant lapsed no later than that day; recorded as 1961-01-03 inclusive, with the exclusive reading (end when that day begins) disclosed as the alternative. The end source is the order's own operative text. Later event: see the later_events entry, which amends the paragraph but leaves the Congress limit unchanged.

Eisenhower on November 27, 1959. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Inspection of Income Tax Returns by the Senate Committee on the Judiciary). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: the order is one grant, a single sentence opening income tax (years 1945 to 1958, inclusive, as the order first read; Executive Order 10876 later changed the closing year to 1959) returns to inspection by the Senate Committee on the Judiciary or any duly authorized subcommittee, followed by a sentence fixing its effective date on filing for publication. The grant is limited by its own words to the period of the Eighty-sixth Congress, which I treat as the order's fixed term. The terms of the Members of the Eighty-sixth Congress began at noon on January 3, 1959 and ended at noon on January 3, 1961 (Twentieth Amendment, sections 1 and 2). The Constitution is not among the held texts and no held source states that date, so the end date rests on that constitutional text together with the order's own words; no other source is claimed for it. First end: January 3, 1961 by the order's own terms, recorded inclusive. The exclusive reading (the end when that day begins) is the alternative the owner ruling requires me to disclose, but it fits poorly here because the Congress's terms ran until noon of that day. Later event: Executive Order 10876, signed April 22, 1960 (25 FR 3569), amends the first paragraph of this order by deleting the years 1945 to 1958 and inserting 1945 to 1959, and by inserting a reference to Senate Resolution 238, 86th Congress, agreed to February 8, 1960; it takes effect on filing for publication, and its Register filing line gives April 25, 1960. This is a strike-and-insert amendment, so the clause continues, amended, and the amendment does not touch the Eighty-sixth Congress limit; the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments is applied. The dossier's two leads for Executive Orders 10850 and 10854 (cited by number, no change provision located) are held Register page texts that print this order's heading on a shared page with those neighbouring orders; they do not change it. The three chosen machine searches state their coverage with no warning and their coverage notes were read. The U.S. Code and eCFR searches returned no hit for this order; the later-events search returned the hits recorded as Executive Order 10876 (the amendment recorded as a later event below) and no other change.

Executive Order 10852
AMENDMENT OF EXECUTIVE ORDER  
NO. 10530,1  PROVIDING FOR THE  
PERFORMANCE OF CERTAIN FUNC­
TIONS VESTED IN OR SUBJECT TO  
THE APPROVAL OF THE PRESIDENT
By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by section 301 of title 3 of the United 
States Code, and as President of the 
United States, it is ordered that Execu­
tive Order No. 10530 of May 10, 1954, 
entitled “Providing for the Performance 
of Certain Functions Vested in or Sub­
ject to the Approval of the President,” 
be, and it is hereby, amended by delet­
ing from section 4(b) thereof the words 
“capital grants with respect to projects 
assisted under Title I  of the said act” and 
inserting in lieu thereof the following: 
“grants under Title I of that act”.

Executive Order 10853
DELEGATING THE AUTHORITY OF  
THE PRESIDENT WITH RESPECT  
TO VARIOUS ALLOWANCES TO  
CERTAIN GOVERNMENT PERSON­
NEL ON FOREIGN DUTY
By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by section 7(a) and 8(a) of the Defense 
Department Overseas Teachers Pay and 
Personnel Practices Act (73 Stat. 216) 
and by section 235(a) of title 38 of the 
United States Code, and as President of 
the United States, it is ordered as 
follows:
119 FR. 2709; 3 CFR, 1954 Supp., p. 55.
S e c t io n 1. The regulations contained in 
Executive Order No. 10000 of September 
16, 1948, as now or hereafter amended, 
which govern the payment of additional 
compensation in foreign areas (referred 
to as foreign post differential) shall gov­
ern the payment of the additional com­
pensation authorized by section 8(a)(2) 
of the Defense Department Overseas 
Teachers Pay and Personnel Practices 
Act of 1959, subject to the provisions of 
section 8(b) of that act (73 Stat. 216).
S ec. 2. Paragraph 1 of Executive Or­
der No. 10011 of October 22, 1948, as 
amended, is hereby further amended by 
adding the following subsections (e) and 
(f ) at the end thereof:
“ (e) The authority vested in the Presi­
dent by section 7 (a) of the Defense De­
partment Overseas Teachers Pay and 
Personnel Practices Act (73 Stat. 216) 
to prescribe regulations relating to quar­
ters, quarters allowance, and storage, 
and the authority vested in the President 
by section 8(a) (1) of that act to pre­
scribe regulations relating to cost-of- 
living allowances.
“(f)  The authority vested in the 
President by section 235(a) of title 38 
of the United States Code to prescribe 
rules and regulations with respect to al­
lowances and benefits similar to those 
provided by those sections of the Foreign 
Service Act of 1946 designated in para­
graphs (1), (2), (3), (5), (6), and (8) 
of section 235(a).”
S ec . 3. The Administrator of Veterans’ 
Affairs is hereby authorized to exercise 
the authority vested in the President by 
section 235(a) of title 38 of the United 
States Code to prescribe rules and regu­
lations with respect to allowances and 
benefits similar to those provided by 
those sections of the Foreign Service Act 
of 1946 designated in paragraphs (4) and 
(7) of section 235(a).
Sec. 4. The rules and regulations pre­
scribed by the Secretary of State or the 
Administrator of Veterans’ Affairs pur­
suant to section 2 or section 3 of this 
order shall become effective on such 
dates as those officials shall, respectively, 
determine, but not in any case earlier 
than July 28, 1959.
D w ig h t D. E ise n h o w e r
T h e W h it e H o use,
November 27, 1959.
[F.R. Doc. 59-10139; Filed, Nov. 30, 1959;
9:34 a.m.]
Executive O rder . 10854 *
EXTENSION OF THE APPLICATION OF  
THE FEDERAL AVIATION ACT OF  
1958
By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by section 1110 of the Federal Aviation 
Act of 1958 (72 Stat. 800; 49 U.S.C. 
1510), and as President of the United 
States, and having determined that such 
action would be in the national interest, 
I  hereby order as follows:
The application of the Federal Avia­
tion Act of 1958 (72 Stat. 731; 49 U.S.C.
1301 et seq.), to the ^extent necessary to 
permit the Administrator of the Federal 
Aviation Agency to accomplish the pur­
poses and objectives of Titles n i and X II 
thereof (49 U.S.C. 1341-1355 and 1521- 
1523), is hereby extended to those areas 
of land or water outside the United 
States and the overlying airspace thereof 
over or in which the Federal Govern­
ment of the United States, under inter­
national treaty, agreement or other 
lawful arrangement, has appropriate 
jurisdiction or control: Provided,  that 
the Administrator, prior to taking any 
action under the authority hereby con­
ferred, shall first consult with the Sec­
retary of State on matters affecting 
foreign relations, and with the Secre­
tary of Defense on matters affecting 
national-defense interests, and shall not 
take any action which the Secretary of 
State determines to be in conflict with 
any international treaty or agreement to 
which the United States is a party, or 
to be inconsistent with the successful 
conduct of the-foreign relations of the 
United States, or which the Secretary of 
Defense determines to be inconsistent 
with the requirements of national de­
fense.
D w ig h t D. E ise n h o w e r
T h e W h it e H o use,
November 27, 1959.
[F.R. Doc. 59-10140; Filed, Nov. 30, 1959;
9:35 a.m.]
Executive Order 10855
INSPECTION OF INCOME TAX RE­
TURNS BY THE SENATE COMMIT­
TEE ON THE JUDICIARY
By virtue of the authority vested In 
me by sections 55(a) and 508 of the In­
ternal Revenue Code of 1939 (53 Stat. 
29, 111; 54 Stat. 1008; 26 U.S.C. 55(a) 
and 508), and by section 6103(a) of the 
Internal Revenue Code of 1954 (68A Stat. 
753; 26 U.S.C. 6103(a)), it is hereby or­
dered that any income tax return for the 
years 1945 to 1958, inclusive, shall, dur­
ing the Eighty-sixth Congress, be open 
to inspection by the Senate Committee 
on the Judiciary, or any duly authorized 
subcommittee thereof, in connection 
with its study and investigation of the 
applicability of the antitrust and anti- 
monopoly laws of the United States to 
professional boxing, pursuant to Senate 
Resolution 57, 86th Congress, agreed to 
February 2, 1959, such inspection to be 
in accordance and upon compliance with 
the rules and regulations prescribed by 
the Secretary of the Treasury in Treas­
ury Decisions 6132 and 6133, relating to 
the inspection of returns by committees 
of the Congress, approved by me on May 
3,1955.
This order shall be effective upon its 
filing for publication in the F ederal  
R egister .
D w ig h t D. E is e n h o w e r
T h e W h it e H o u se,
November 27, 1959.
[F.R. Doc. 59-10141; Filed, Nov. 30, 1959;
9:35 a.m.l /

Approval of Air Carrier Training Pro­
grams; Qualification of Pilots Other 
Than Pilots in Command; Proficiency 
Checks for Pilots Other Than Pilots  
in Command
The Federal Aviation Agency pub­
lish ed  as a notice of rule making (24 F.R, 
5246) and circulated as Civil Air Regula­
tion s Draft Release No. 59-3, dated June 
tu’  a Pr°P°sal to amend Part 40 oi  
th e Civil Air Regulations to require: (1)  
™ A A  approval of air carrier training pro­
grams; (2) appropriate aircraft ratings  
tor pilots serving as other than pilots in  
oottunand; and (3) more specific initia]  
training and recurrent proficiency checks 
*°r pilots serving as other than pilots in
command.
Interested persons have been afforded  
opportunity to participate in the mak-  
t?? this amendment and due qpnsider-  
«tion has been given to all relevant  
“tatter presented. Because of the im­
portance of this amendment, each por-  
thereof has been evaluated in the  
“Sht of such comments.
1. FAA approval o f air carrier training  
program s.  The air carriers commenting  
on this portion of the proposal expressed  
strong opposition to it. Briefly, the air  
carriers contend that the present regu­
latory scheme for the establishment of  
methods and procedures for crew mem­
ber training programs has been adequate  
and that no justification has been shown  
for requiring FAA approval of such pro­
grams. The FAA is unable to agree with  
these contentions.
It must be emphasized that the train­
ing program is one of the most important  
factorsJn the safety of air carrier opera­
tions. The quality and scope of such  
programs are the key to insuring that  
all crew members are competent to per­
form their duties with the high degree  
of skill expected and required in air car­
rier operations. Under the provisions  
of the present regulation, the air carriers  
are given discretion in establishing “ade­
quate” or “appropriate” training, or  
“training as necessary.” As a result  
some air carriers have prepared and are  
administering excellent training pro­
grams. However, others have not  
achieved the minimum safety objective  
sought by the training requirements of  
§§ 40.280 through 40.289. While the  
methods and procedures employed by the  
various air carriers in their training pro­
grams may differ to fit the particular  
operation of each air carrier, each train­
ing program must provide a uniform and  
minimum standard of flight and ground  
training necessary for safety in air trans­
portation. Experience in the adminis-
tration of the present regulations shows  
that this standard can only be achieved  
by FAA approval of each training pro­
gram.
Accordingly, because of the vital im­
portance which the air carrier training  
program has to safety in air carrier oper­
ations, each air carrier subject to this  
part will be required to obtain approval  
of its training program by a representa­
tive of the Administrator.
This final regulation will not alter the  
responsibility which each air carrier has  
at present for the preparation and ad­
ministration of its training program.  
However, each air carrier will be required  
Ç o  submit its training program, and sub­
sequent changes thereto, to the FAA for  
prior approval.
2. Initial training qualifications o f  
pilots other than  pilots in com m and.  
The complexity of modern aircraft and  
the operational demands of today’s navi­
gation, communication, and air traffic  
control systems require a high level of  
skill and competance for air „carrier co­
pilots. Many of the functions which are  
required of the copilot, particularly with  
respect to emergency procedures, must  
be performed properly or the safety of  
the flight may be seriously affected. In  
addition, in the event that the pilot in  
command becomes incapacitated during  
flight, the copilot must possess adequate  
knowledge and skill to fly the aircraft  
safely to a destination.
In order to properly determine the  
ability of the copilot to operate a partic­
ular type of aircraft, it was proposed in  
Draft Release 59-3 to provide for the  
issuance of appropriate aircraft type  
ratings for all pilots serving as other  
than pilots in command. However,  
upon réévaluation of the original pro­
posal in the light of comments received,  
it appears that the objective of the orig­
inal proposal can be achieved without  
requiring pilots serving other than as  
pilots in command to obtain an appropri­
ate aircraft type rating, provided ade­
quate flight training for those pilots who  
serve as second in command is provided  
in the initial and recurrent training re­
quirements of this part and is part of the  
training., program approved by the  
Administrator.
Accordingly, the original proposal has  
been modified in this regulation by omit­
ting the aircraft type rating require­
ment. In lieu of a type rating, this  
regulation prescribes in §  40.282(c) cer­
tain minimum maneuvers and proce­
dures in which it is considered necessary  
that pilots serving as second in command  
be proficient, and requires that they re­
ceive instruction and practice in such  
maneuvers and procedures during initial  
flight training.
The term “second in command” is used

By the President of the United States

A Proclamation
WHEREAS December 15, 1959, marks  
the one hundred and sixty-eighth anni­
versary of the adoption of our Bill of  
Rights, the first ten amendments to the  
Constitution of the United States; and  
WHEREAS December 10, 1959, marks  
the eleventh anniversary of the adoption  
by the General Assembly of the United  
Nations of the Universal Declaration of  
Human Rights; and  
WHEREAS the individual rights and  
freedoms set forth in the Bill of Rights  
constitute a vital part of the political  
heritage of each American citizen; and

and freedoms declared in the Universal  
D eclaration of Human Rights is a  basic  
objective of the United Nations:

States of America, do hereby proclaim  
the period of December 10 to Decem­
ber 17,1959, as Human Rights Week, and  
I call upon the citizens of the United  
States to observe these anniversaries by  
studying the Bill of Rights of the United  
States and the Universal Declaration of  
Human Rights of the United Nations,  
that we may grow in our understanding  
°f the inherent dignity and the equal  
and inalienable rights of each member  
of the humari family. In gratitude for  
the liberties that we enjoy, let us work  
to advance universal freedom and justice  
stand ready to uphold the rights of  
ethers which are inextricably linked  
W ith  our own.

hereunto set my hand and caused the  
® eal of the United States of America to  
b e affixed.

Approval of Air Carrier Training Pro­
grams; Qualification of Pilots Other 
Than Pilots in Command; Proficiency 
Checks for Pilots Other Than Pilots  
in Command
The Federal Aviation Agency pub­
lish ed  as a notice of rule making (24 F.R, 
5246) and circulated as Civil Air Regula­
tion s Draft Release No. 59-3, dated June 
tu’  a Pr°P°sal to amend Part 40 oi  
th e Civil Air Regulations to require: (1)  
™ A A  approval of air carrier training pro­
grams; (2) appropriate aircraft ratings  
tor pilots serving as other than pilots in  
oottunand; and (3) more specific initia]  
training and recurrent proficiency checks 
*°r pilots serving as other than pilots in
command.
Interested persons have been afforded  
opportunity to participate in the mak-  
t?? this amendment and due qpnsider-  
«tion has been given to all relevant  
“tatter presented. Because of the im­
portance of this amendment, each por-  
thereof has been evaluated in the  
“Sht of such comments.
1. FAA approval o f air carrier training  
program s.  The air carriers commenting  
on this portion of the proposal expressed  
strong opposition to it. Briefly, the air  
carriers contend that the present regu­
latory scheme for the establishment of  
methods and procedures for crew mem­
ber training programs has been adequate  
and that no justification has been shown  
for requiring FAA approval of such pro­
grams. The FAA is unable to agree with  
these contentions.
It must be emphasized that the train­
ing program is one of the most important  
factorsJn the safety of air carrier opera­
tions. The quality and scope of such  
programs are the key to insuring that  
all crew members are competent to per­
form their duties with the high degree  
of skill expected and required in air car­
rier operations. Under the provisions  
of the present regulation, the air carriers  
are given discretion in establishing “ade­
quate” or “appropriate” training, or  
“training as necessary.” As a result  
some air carriers have prepared and are  
administering excellent training pro­
grams. However, others have not  
achieved the minimum safety objective  
sought by the training requirements of  
§§ 40.280 through 40.289. While the  
methods and procedures employed by the  
various air carriers in their training pro­
grams may differ to fit the particular  
operation of each air carrier, each train­
ing program must provide a uniform and  
minimum standard of flight and ground  
training necessary for safety in air trans­
portation. Experience in the adminis-
tration of the present regulations shows  
that this standard can only be achieved  
by FAA approval of each training pro­
gram.
Accordingly, because of the vital im­
portance which the air carrier training  
program has to safety in air carrier oper­
ations, each air carrier subject to this  
part will be required to obtain approval  
of its training program by a representa­
tive of the Administrator.
This final regulation will not alter the  
responsibility which each air carrier has  
at present for the preparation and ad­
ministration of its training program.  
However, each air carrier will be required  
Ç o  submit its training program, and sub­
sequent changes thereto, to the FAA for  
prior approval.
2. Initial training qualifications o f  
pilots other than  pilots in com m and.  
The complexity of modern aircraft and  
the operational demands of today’s navi­
gation, communication, and air traffic  
control systems require a high level of  
skill and competance for air „carrier co­
pilots. Many of the functions which are  
required of the copilot, particularly with  
respect to emergency procedures, must  
be performed properly or the safety of  
the flight may be seriously affected. In  
addition, in the event that the pilot in  
command becomes incapacitated during  
flight, the copilot must possess adequate  
knowledge and skill to fly the aircraft  
safely to a destination.
In order to properly determine the  
ability of the copilot to operate a partic­
ular type of aircraft, it was proposed in  
Draft Release 59-3 to provide for the  
issuance of appropriate aircraft type  
ratings for all pilots serving as other  
than pilots in command. However,  
upon réévaluation of the original pro­
posal in the light of comments received,  
it appears that the objective of the orig­
inal proposal can be achieved without  
requiring pilots serving other than as  
pilots in command to obtain an appropri­
ate aircraft type rating, provided ade­
quate flight training for those pilots who  
serve as second in command is provided  
in the initial and recurrent training re­
quirements of this part and is part of the  
training., program approved by the  
Administrator.
Accordingly, the original proposal has  
been modified in this regulation by omit­
ting the aircraft type rating require­
ment. In lieu of a type rating, this  
regulation prescribes in §  40.282(c) cer­
tain minimum maneuvers and proce­
dures in which it is considered necessary  
that pilots serving as second in command  
be proficient, and requires that they re­
ceive instruction and practice in such  
maneuvers and procedures during initial  
flight training.
The term “second in command” is used  
in this regulation in order to identify  
more precisely those pilots who perform  
the traditional functions of a copilot, as  
distinguished from the pilot in command  
and other pilots. In this respect, this  
regulation amends current §  40.261(c) to  
make it clear that where the air carrier  
is authorized to operate under instru­
