HUMAN RIGHTS WEEK, 1959  
By the President of the United States  
of America  
A Proclamation
WHEREAS December 15, 1959, marks  
the one hundred and sixty-eighth anni­
versary of the adoption of our Bill of  
Rights, the first ten amendments to the  
Constitution of the United States; and  
WHEREAS December 10, 1959, marks  
the eleventh anniversary of the adoption  
by the General Assembly of the United  
Nations of the Universal Declaration of  
Human Rights; and  
WHEREAS the individual rights and  
freedoms set forth in the Bill of Rights  
constitute a vital part of the political  
heritage of each American citizen; and  
WHEREAS promotion of the rights  
and freedoms declared in the Universal  
D eclaration of Human Rights is a  basic  
objective of the United Nations:
NOW, THEREFORE, I, DWIGHT D.  
EISENHOWER, President of the United  
States of America, do hereby proclaim  
the period of December 10 to Decem­
ber 17,1959, as Human Rights Week, and  
I call upon the citizens of the United  
States to observe these anniversaries by  
studying the Bill of Rights of the United  
States and the Universal Declaration of  
Human Rights of the United Nations,  
that we may grow in our understanding  
°f the inherent dignity and the equal  
and inalienable rights of each member  
of the humari family. In gratitude for  
the liberties that we enjoy, let us work  
to advance universal freedom and justice  
stand ready to uphold the rights of  
ethers which are inextricably linked  
W ith  our own.
T N  WITNESS WHEREOF, I  have  
hereunto set my hand and caused the  
® eal of the United States of America to  
b e affixed.
DONE at the City of Washington this  
third day of December in the year of  
our Lord nineteen hundred and  
[ seal ] fifty-nine, and of the Independ­
ence of the United States of  
America the one hundred and eighty-  
fourth.
D w ight D. E isenhower  
By the President:

Executive Order 10856
EXCUSING FEDERAL  EMPLOYEES  
FROM DUTY FOR ONE-HALF DAY  
ON DECEMBER 24, 1959
By virtue of the authority vested in me  
as President of the United States, it is  
hereby ordered that employees of the  
several executive departments, inde­
pendent establishments, and other gov­
ernmental agencies, including the Gen­
eral Accounting Office, the Government  
Printing Office, and the field services of  
the respective departments, establish­
ments, and agencies of the Government,  
except those who may for special public  
reasons be excluded from the provisions  
of this order by the heads of their re­
spective departments, establishments, or  
agencies, or those whose absence from  
duty would be inconsistent with the pro­
visions of existing law, shall be excused  
from duty for one-half day on Thursday,  
December 24, 1959, the day preceding  
Christmas Day; and such one-half day  
shall be considered a holiday within the  
meaning of Executive Order No. 10358 of  
June 9,1952, and of all statutes so far as  
they relate to the compensation and  
leave of employees of the United States.
The heads of departments, agencies,  
and independent establishments shall,^ to 
the extent consistent with the needs of  
the service, adopt a liberal policy for the  
granting of annual leave to all employees  
(Continued on p. 9765)

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10856 (24 FR 9763, PDF pages 1-3; Federal Register issue of December 5, 1959; govinfo PDF text layer held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10856.txt), headed Executive Order 10856, signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower on December 3, 1959. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Excusing Federal Employees From Duty One-Half Day on December 24, 1959). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: the excusal paragraph excuses covered employees from duty for one-half day on Thursday, December 24, 1959, the day preceding Christmas Day, and treats that half-day as a holiday for the purposes of Executive Order 10358 of June 9, 1952 and of the compensation and leave statutes, with exceptions for employees excluded by agency heads or whose absence would be inconsistent with law. The leave-policy sentence directs agency heads, to the extent consistent with the needs of the service, to adopt a liberal policy for annual leave for employees who wish to take leave over the holiday period; it states no dates. Executive Order 10856
EXCUSING FEDERAL  EMPLOYEES  
FROM DUTY FOR ONE-HALF DAY  
ON DECEMBER 24, 1959
By virtue of the authority vested in me  
as President of the United States, it is  
hereby ordered that employees of the  
several executive departments, inde­
pendent establishments, and other gov­
ernmental agencies, including the Gen­
eral Accounting Office, the Government  
Printing Office, and the field services of  
the respective departments, establish­
ments, and agencies of the Government,  
except those who may for special public  
reasons be excluded from the provisions  
of this order by the heads of their re­
spective departments, establishments, or  
agencies, or those whose absence from  
duty would be inconsistent with the pro­
visions of existing law, shall be excused  
from duty for one-half day on Thursday,  
December 24, 1959, the day preceding  
Christmas Day; and such one-half day  
shall be considered a holiday within the  
meaning of Executive Order No. 10358 of  
June 9,1952, and of all statutes so far as  
they relate to the compensation and  
leave of employees of the United States.
The heads of departments, agencies,  
and independent establishments shall,^ to 
the extent consistent with the needs of  
the service, adopt a liberal policy for the  
granting of annual leave to all employees

Interested persons have been afforded  
opportunity to participate in the mak-  
t?? this amendment and due qpnsider-  
«tion has been given to all relevant  
“tatter presented. Because of the im­
portance of this amendment, each por-  
thereof has been evaluated in the

1. FAA approval o f air carrier training  
program s.  The air carriers commenting  
on this portion of the proposal expressed  
strong opposition to it. Briefly, the air  
carriers contend that the present regu­
latory scheme for the establishment of  
methods and procedures for crew mem­
ber training programs has been adequate  
and that no justification has been shown  
for requiring FAA approval of such pro­
grams. The FAA is unable to agree with  
these contentions.
It must be emphasized that the train­
ing program is one of the most important  
factorsJn the safety of air carrier opera­
tions. The quality and scope of such  
programs are the key to insuring that  
all crew members are competent to per­
form their duties with the high degree  
of skill expected and required in air car­
rier operations. Under the provisions  
of the present regulation, the air carriers  
are given discretion in establishing “ade­
quate” or “appropriate” training, or  
“training as necessary.” As a result  
some air carriers have prepared and are  
administering excellent training pro­
grams. However, others have not  
achieved the minimum safety objective  
sought by the training requirements of  
§§ 40.280 through 40.289. While the  
methods and procedures employed by the  
various air carriers in their training pro­
grams may differ to fit the particular  
operation of each air carrier, each train­
ing program must provide a uniform and  
minimum standard of flight and ground  
training necessary for safety in air trans­
portation. Experience in the adminis-
tration of the present regulations shows  
that this standard can only be achieved  
by FAA approval of each training pro­
gram.
Accordingly, because of the vital im­
portance which the air carrier training  
program has to safety in air carrier oper­
ations, each air carrier subject to this  
part will be required to obtain approval  
of its training program by a representa­
tive of the Administrator.
This final regulation will not alter the  
responsibility which each air carrier has  
at present for the preparation and ad­
ministration of its training program.  
However, each air carrier will be required  
Ç o  submit its training program, and sub­
sequent changes thereto, to the FAA for  
prior approval.
2. Initial training qualifications o f  
pilots other than  pilots in com m and.  
The complexity of modern aircraft and  
the operational demands of today’s navi­
gation, communication, and air traffic  
control systems require a high level of  
skill and competance for air „carrier co­
pilots. Many of the functions which are  
required of the copilot, particularly with  
respect to emergency procedures, must  
be performed properly or the safety of  
the flight may be seriously affected. In  
addition, in the event that the pilot in  
command becomes incapacitated during  
flight, the copilot must possess adequate  
knowledge and skill to fly the aircraft  
safely to a destination.
In order to properly determine the  
ability of the copilot to operate a partic­
ular type of aircraft, it was proposed in  
Draft Release 59-3 to provide for the  
issuance of appropriate aircraft type  
ratings for all pilots serving as other  
than pilots in command. However,  
upon réévaluation of the original pro­
posal in the light of comments received,

inal proposal can be achieved without  
requiring pilots serving other than as  
pilots in command to obtain an appropri­
ate aircraft type rating, provided ade­
quate flight training for those pilots who  
serve as second in command is provided  
in the initial and recurrent training re­
quirements of this part and is part of the  
training., program approved by the  
Administrator.

been modified in this regulation by omit­
ting the aircraft type rating require­
ment. In lieu of a type rating, this  
regulation prescribes in §  40.282(c) cer­
tain minimum maneuvers and proce­
dures in which it is considered necessary  
that pilots serving as second in command  
be proficient, and requires that they re­
ceive instruction and practice in such  
maneuvers and procedures during initial  
flight training.

in Command
The Federal Aviation Agency pub­
lish ed  as a notice of rule making (24 F.R, 
5246) and circulated as Civil Air Regula­
tion s Draft Release No. 59-3, dated June 
tu’  a Pr°P°sal to amend Part 40 oi  
th e Civil Air Regulations to require: (1)  
™ A A  approval of air carrier training pro­
grams; (2) appropriate aircraft ratings  
tor pilots serving as other than pilots in  
oottunand; and (3) more specific initia]  
training and recurrent proficiency checks 
*°r pilots serving as other than pilots in
command.
Interested persons have been afforded  
opportunity to participate in the mak-  
t?? this amendment and due qpnsider-  
«tion has been given to all relevant  
“tatter presented. Because of the im­
portance of this amendment, each por-  
thereof has been evaluated in the  
“Sht of such comments.
1. FAA approval o f air carrier training  
program s.  The air carriers commenting  
on this portion of the proposal expressed  
strong opposition to it. Briefly, the air  
carriers contend that the present regu­
latory scheme for the establishment of  
methods and procedures for crew mem­
ber training programs has been adequate  
and that no justification has been shown  
for requiring FAA approval of such pro­
grams. The FAA is unable to agree with  
these contentions.
It must be emphasized that the train­
ing program is one of the most important  
factorsJn the safety of air carrier opera­
tions. The quality and scope of such  
programs are the key to insuring that  
all crew members are competent to per­
form their duties with the high degree  
of skill expected and required in air car­
rier operations. Under the provisions  
of the present regulation, the air carriers  
are given discretion in establishing “ade­
quate” or “appropriate” training, or  
“training as necessary.” As a result  
some air carriers have prepared and are  
administering excellent training pro­
grams. However, others have not  
achieved the minimum safety objective  
sought by the training requirements of  
§§ 40.280 through 40.289. While the  
methods and procedures employed by the  
various air carriers in their training pro­
grams may differ to fit the particular  
operation of each air carrier, each train­
ing program must provide a uniform and  
minimum standard of flight and ground  
training necessary for safety in air trans­
portation. Experience in the adminis-
tration of the present regulations shows  
that this standard can only be achieved  
by FAA approval of each training pro­
gram.
Accordingly, because of the vital im­
portance which the air carrier training  
program has to safety in air carrier oper­
ations, each air carrier subject to this  
part will be required to obtain approval  
of its training program by a representa­
tive of the Administrator.
This final regulation will not alter the  
responsibility which each air carrier has  
at present for the preparation and ad­
ministration of its training program.  
However, each air carrier will be required  
Ç o  submit its training program, and sub­
sequent changes thereto, to the FAA for  
prior approval.
2. Initial training qualifications o f  
pilots other than  pilots in com m and.  
The complexity of modern aircraft and  
the operational demands of today’s navi­
gation, communication, and air traffic  
control systems require a high level of  
skill and competance for air „carrier co­
pilots. Many of the functions which are  
required of the copilot, particularly with  
respect to emergency procedures, must  
be performed properly or the safety of  
the flight may be seriously affected. In  
addition, in the event that the pilot in  
command becomes incapacitated during  
flight, the copilot must possess adequate  
knowledge and skill to fly the aircraft  
safely to a destination.
In order to properly determine the  
ability of the copilot to operate a partic­
ular type of aircraft, it was proposed in  
Draft Release 59-3 to provide for the  
issuance of appropriate aircraft type  
ratings for all pilots serving as other  
than pilots in command. However,  
upon réévaluation of the original pro­
posal in the light of comments received,  
it appears that the objective of the orig­
inal proposal can be achieved without  
requiring pilots serving other than as  
pilots in command to obtain an appropri­
ate aircraft type rating, provided ade­
quate flight training for those pilots who  
serve as second in command is provided  
in the initial and recurrent training re­
quirements of this part and is part of the  
training., program approved by the  
Administrator.
Accordingly, the original proposal has  
been modified in this regulation by omit­
ting the aircraft type rating require­
ment. In lieu of a type rating, this  
regulation prescribes in §  40.282(c) cer­
tain minimum maneuvers and proce­
dures in which it is considered necessary  
that pilots serving as second in command  
be proficient, and requires that they re­
ceive instruction and practice in such  
maneuvers and procedures during initial  
flight training.
The term “second in command” is used  
in this regulation in order to identify

distinguished from the pilot in command

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Exhausted by performance on February 5, 1960, the date the order was signed. Its only operative words revoke Executive Order No. 10758 of March 4, 1958, which established a career executive program within the civil-service system, and Executive Order No. 10777 of August 6, 1958, which amended it to increase the membership of the Career Executive Board, a one-time act that commands nothing afterwards. The order has no effective-date wording, so it is read as effective when signed; the Federal Register issue of February 9, 1960 is the alternative reading and is disclosed here. Actor: the order itself; the end source is its own operative text. The revoked order's non-operation is the surviving consequence, not a continuing command.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10859 (25 FR 1089, PDF pages 1-4; Federal Register issue of February 9, 1960; govinfo PDF text layer held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10859.txt), headed Executive Order 10859, signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower on February 5, 1960. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Revocation of Executive Order 10758 Establishing a Career Executive Program Within the Civil Service System, and Executive Order 10777, Amending Executive Order 10758). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: the order has one operative sentence, the revocation of Executive Order No. 10758 of March 4, 1958, which established a career executive program within the civil-service system, and Executive Order No. 10777 of August 6, 1958, which amended it to increase the membership of the Career Executive Board. The single sentence revokes two orders at once; I keep them in one clause because both are revoked by the same words on the same day. The order states no effective date, so it took effect when signed on February 5, 1960; the Federal Register printed it on February 9, 1960, which is the alternative date a reader might take for effectiveness. The revocation is a single act that the order performs by its own words when it issues; once made it commands nothing further, so the clause is exhausted by performance on the signing date. What survives is the fact that the revoked order no longer operates, which is a consequence of the act and not a continuing command of this order. Title 3— THE PRESIDENT
Executive Order 10871
INSPECTION OF INCOME, EXCESS-  
PROFITS, ESTATE, AND GIFT TAX  
RETURNS BY THE HOUSE COM­
MITTEE ON PUBLIC WORKS
By virtue of the authority vested in 
me by sections 55(a) and 508 of the 
Internal Revenue Code of 1939 (53 Stat. 
29, 111; 54 Stat. 1008; 26 U.S.C. 55(a) 
and 5Q8), and by section 6103(a) of the 
Internal Revenue Code of 1954 (68A 
Stat. 753; 26 U.S.C. 6103(a) ), it is hereby 
ordered that any income, excess-profits, 
estate, or gift tax return for the years 
1950 to 1959, inclusive, shall, during the 
Eighty-sixth Congress, be open to in­
spection by the House Committee on 
Public Works, or any duly authorized 
subcommittee thereof, in connection 
with its investigation of the policies, pro­
cedures and practices involved in the 
administration of the Federal-aid high­
way program, pursuant to House Resolu­
tion 91,86th Congress, agreed to January 
29,1959, such inspection to be in accord­
ance and upon compliance with the rules 
and regulations prescribed by the Secre­
tary of the Treasury in Treasury Deci­
sions 6132 and 6133, relating to the in­
spection of returns by committees of the 
Congress, approved by me on May 3,1955.
This order shall be effective upon its 
filing for publication in the F ederal  
R egister .
D w ig h t D. E is e n h o w e r
T h e W h it e H o u s e,
March 15,1960.
[F.R. Doc. 60-2515; Filed, Mar. 16, 1960;
4:31 p.m.]

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by its own terms at the end of the Eighty-sixth Congress. Executive Order 10871, signed March 15, 1960 (25 FR 2251, PDF pages 3-3), orders that income, excess-profits, estate and gift tax (years 1950 to 1959, inclusive) returns shall, during the Eighty-sixth Congress, be open to inspection by the House Committee on Public Works, or any duly authorized subcommittee, in connection with its investigation of the policies, procedures and practices of the Federal-aid highway program, pursuant to House Resolution 91, 86th Congress, agreed to January 29, 1959. The order sets no other term, condition or revocation clause. The terms of the Members of the Eighty-sixth Congress ended at noon on January 3, 1961 under the Twentieth Amendment, so the grant lapsed no later than that day; recorded as 1961-01-03 inclusive, with the exclusive reading (end when that day begins) disclosed as the alternative. The end source is the order's own operative text. No later amending event is held.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10871 (25 FR 2251, PDF pages 3-3; Federal Register issue of March 18, 1960; govinfo PDF text layer held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10871.txt), headed Executive Order 10871, signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower on March 15, 1960. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Inspection of Income, Excess-Profits, Estate, and Gift Tax returns by the House Committee on Public Works). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: the order is one grant, a single sentence opening income, excess-profits, estate and gift tax (years 1950 to 1959, inclusive) returns to inspection by the House Committee on Public Works or any duly authorized subcommittee, followed by a sentence fixing its effective date on filing for publication. The grant is limited by its own words to the period of the Eighty-sixth Congress, which I treat as the order's fixed term. The terms of the Members of the Eighty-sixth Congress began at noon on January 3, 1959 and ended at noon on January 3, 1961 (Twentieth Amendment, sections 1 and 2). The Constitution is not among the held texts and no held source states that date, so the end date rests on that constitutional text together with the order's own words; no other source is claimed for it. First end: January 3, 1961 by the order's own terms, recorded inclusive. The exclusive reading (the end when that day begins) is the alternative the owner ruling requires me to disclose, but it fits poorly here because the Congress's terms ran until noon of that day. The three chosen machine searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes plus operative sentences of 17521 saved order texts) each state their coverage with no warning; their coverage notes were read. They search by this order's number, and none returned a hit for it.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The purpose the order states (House Resolution 91, 86th Congress) explains why the committee may inspect and is not a limit on the grant's term; no held text shows that purpose withdrawn or exhausted before the Congress ended. (2) The recital of Treasury Decisions 6132 and 6133 governs how inspection proceeds and sets no end. (3) The effective-date sentence starts the grant and is not an end. (4) The Cruden number lookup in LOOKUPS.md (all held order texts except clause drafts) finds this number only in the held Federal Register text of this order itself. An exact-number search of the held text of EO 12553 (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_12553.txt, the 1986 mass revocation table) finds no entry for this number. No other instrument is shown to have revoked, superseded or terminated the grant before January 3, 1961.","independent_command_check":"The order commands nothing independent of the inspection grant: the Treasury Decisions recital sets the manner of inspection and the effective-date sentence is not a command. No appointment, delegation or direction to an agency survives the grant.","savings_check":"The order has no saving wording. Inspections already made are completed acts that rest on the grant and do not keep it operative after January 3, 1961.","scope_check":"The order has one operative clause and it ends in full on January 3, 1961. The dossier inventory (one whole-order clause) is complete."}

savings_residuals.reason: The order contains no savings, exception or transitional clause; I read its whole text for such wording. Any inspection made while the grant ran is a completed act, and nothing in the order continues the grant after the Eighty-sixth Congress ended. Any later statutory change to the Internal Revenue Code sections the order cites would postdate this end and cannot be a first end.

By virtue of the authority vested in me as President of the United 
States and as Commander in Chief of the Armed Forces of the United

Badge” are hereby amended to read as follows:

hereby reestablished as the Presidential Service Certificate, to be 
awarded in the name of the President of the United States to members 
of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, and Coast Guard who 
have been assigned to the White House Office or to military units 
and support facilities under the administration of the Military Assist­
ant to the President for a period of at least one year subsequent to 
J  anuary 20,1969.
“3. Badge established. The White House Service Badge is replaced 
by the Presidential Service Badge, the design of which accompanies 
and is hereby made a part of this Order. The Presidential Service 
Badge may be awarded to any member of the Armed Forces assigned 
to duty in the White House Office or to military units and support 
facilities under the administration of the Military Assistant to the 
President by the Secretary of the Army, the Secretary of the Navy, 
the Secretary of the Air Force, or, when the Coast Guard is not oper­
ating as a service in the Navy, the Secretary of Transportation, upon 
recommendation of the Military Assistant to the President, to military 
personnel of their respective services. The Badge may be worn as a 
part of the uniform of those individuals upon award of the Presi­
dential Service Certificate under such regulations as the Secretary of 
the Army, the Secretary of the Navy, and the Secretary of the Air 
Force, with the approval of the Secretary of Defense, and, when the 
Coast Guard is not operating as a service in the Navy, the Commandant 
of the Coast Guard, with the approval of the Secretary of Trans­
portation, may severally prescribe.”

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10879 (25 FR 4893, PDF pages 3-3; Federal Register issue of June 3, 1960; govinfo PDF text layer held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10879.txt), headed Executive Order 10879, signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower on June 1, 1960. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Establishing the White House Service Certificate and the White House Service Badge). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: five numbered paragraphs, which the dossier lists as five clauses, and the badge design that paragraph 3 makes part of the order (a figure, not a clause); I confirm the inventory is complete. Paragraph 1 establishes the White House Service Certificate for members of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps and Air Force, other than Presidential Aides, detailed to White House duty for at least one year after January 20, 1953. Paragraph 2 provides for the certificate's design and for award by the service Secretaries on recommendation of the Presidential Aides. Paragraph 3 establishes the White House Service Badge, which may be worn during the detail. Paragraph 4 limits each person to one certificate. Paragraph 5 allows posthumous award of the certificate. First end: Executive Order 12793, signed March 20, 1992 (57 FR 10281, Federal Register of March 25, 1992), section 5 of which states that it supersedes Executive Order 10879 of June 1, 1960, as amended; it names this order and ends every paragraph. It has no effective-date wording, so it is read as effective when signed. Later events before the end: Executive Order 11174 (September 1, 1964) amended all five numbered paragraphs by restating them; Executive Order 11407 (April 23, 1968) restated paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 of Executive Order 11174; and Executive Order 11520 (March 25, 1970) restated paragraphs 1 and 3 of Executive Order 11407. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments each clause continues, amended, until the parent order ends, so these are later events and not ends; because the 1964 restatement replaced the whole text of every paragraph and the later orders replaced more of paragraphs 1 to 3, the substance of the clauses changed and a human reviewer should read the before and after wording. The dossier's leads for Executive Orders 11407 and 11520 (target provision not located) are resolved by reading their held texts; the current-law lead without an original-source hash is not used. Searches: the three chosen machine searches state their coverage with no warning and their coverage notes were read; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches returned no hit for this order and the later-events search returned the hits recorded here as Executive Orders 11174 and 12793. Executive Order 12793 continues a certificate and badge under the Presidential Service names, but it does so by its own sections 1 and 2 and supersedes this order, so it ends this order and does not extend it.

(2) Executive Orders 11407 and 11520 restate paragraphs of Executive Order 11174, not a command of this order that ends it, and are later events. Its section 5 only supersedes this order and contains no saving or transitional wording for it (I read the whole held text).

Executive Order 10915
AMENDING PRIOR EXECUTIVE OR­

Whereas American agricultural abun­
dance offers a unique opportunity for  
the United States to promote the in­
terests of peace in a significant way and  
to play an important role in helping to  
provide a more adequate diet for peoples  
around the world; and
Whereas exports of farm products are  
of great importance to the domestic  
economy, furnishing approximately 11 
percent of total farm income; and
Whereas many government functions  
and activities relate to the movement  
overseas of agricultural products and  
commodities, and a number of govern­
ment agencies have responsibilities in  
connection with these activities; and
Whereas it is of fundamental im­
portance that we have a national food  
policy directed toward using our agricul­
tural abundance as a national asset to  
meet foreign policy objectives.
NOW , THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me as President of  
the United States, it is ordered as  
follows;

of January 5, 1961 (26 F.R. 143), headed  
“Administration of the Agricultural  
Trade Development and Assistance Act  
of 1954, as amended,” is hereby amended  
by renumbering sections 6 and 7 thereof  
as sections 7 and 8, respectively, and by  
inserting after section 5 the following  
new section 6:

Program.  Subject to the direction of the  
President, the Director of the Food-for-  
Peace Program (provided for in a letter  
of the President bearing the same date  
as this order) shall be responsible for
the continuous supervision and coordi­
nation of the functions hereinabove dele­
gated or otherwise assigned to officers  
or agencies of the Government. The  
foregoing provisions of this section shall  
not be construed as terminating any  
delegation or other assignment of func­

order.”

new section 111, reading as follows;
Sec. 111. Director of the Food-for-

Food-for-Peace Program shall be re­
sponsible for the continuous supervision

shall not be construed as superseding  
any delegation or other assignment of  
function made by the Act or by other

At a session of the Federal Communi­
cations Commission held at its offices in  
Washington, D.C., on the 18th day of  
January 1961;
The Commission has had under con­
sideration the desirability of consolidat­
ing Annual Report Forms O, W ire-tele-  
graph and Ocean-cable Carriers, and R,  
Radiotelegraph Carriers.
The consolidation ordered herein is  
designed to make no change in any re­
porting requirement of substance. The  
separate report form designations, Form  
O, and Form R, are retained but will  
henceforth indicate a single document.  
Certain obsolete schedules or those  
which call for information which ex­
perience has shown the carriers have  
nothing to report on, and are not likely  
to have in the future, have been deleted.
The reporting requirements contained  
in the two annual report forms, Form O  
and Form R, were found to be so similar  
that it seemed a natural step to combine  
them and this similarity made it possible  
to combine many of the schedules in the  
two Forms even to the extent of retain­
ing schedule numbers and titles. There  
are, however, instances of such varia­
tions in the account classifications be­
tween wire-telegraph and ocean-cable,  
on the one hand, and radiotelegraph, on  
the other, that retention of separate re­
porting schedules was found necessary.
The pages of the new combined report  
form are numbered consecutively for  
more ready reference. The size of the  
sheets is the same as in telephone Annual  
Report Form M  prescribed by the Com­
mission and in the Form O  being  
superseded.
Combining of the two report forms  
ordered herein will contribute to. econ­
omy in printing and stocking as com­
pared to the costs of two totally separate  
documents.
A comparative table showing the dis­
position made of the schedules and other  
sheets contained in Forms O  and R  is  
attached to this order .1
It appearing that the consolidation of  
Annual Report Forms O and R  does not  
change in any material respect the re­
porting requirements of the carriers and  
hence that compliance with the public  
notice, procedural, and effective date re­
quirements of section 4 of the Adminis­
trative Procedure Act is unnecessary;  
and
It further appearing that consolida­
tion of the two Forms referred to is  
desirable;

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by its own terms at the end of the Eighty-seventh Congress. Executive Order 10916, signed January 24, 1961 (26 FR 781, PDF pages 3-8), orders that income, estate and gift tax (years 1947 to 1961, inclusive) returns shall, during the Eighty-seventh Congress, be open to inspection by the Senate Committee on Government Operations, or any duly authorized subcommittee, in connection with its studies of the operation of Government activities at all levels with a view to determining the economy and efficiency of the Government. The order sets no other term, condition or revocation clause. The terms of the Members of the Eighty-seventh Congress ended at noon on January 3, 1963 under the Twentieth Amendment, so the grant lapsed no later than that day; recorded as 1963-01-03 inclusive, with the exclusive reading (end when that day begins) disclosed as the alternative. The end source is the order's own operative text. No later amending event is held.

Executive Order 10915
AMENDING PRIOR EXECUTIVE OR­
DERS TO PROVIDE FOR THE RE­
SPONSIBILITIES OF THE DIRECTOR  
OF THE FOOD-FOR-PEACE PRO­
GRAM
Whereas American agricultural abun­
dance offers a unique opportunity for  
the United States to promote the in­
terests of peace in a significant way and  
to play an important role in helping to  
provide a more adequate diet for peoples  
around the world; and
Whereas exports of farm products are  
of great importance to the domestic  
economy, furnishing approximately 11 
percent of total farm income; and
Whereas many government functions  
and activities relate to the movement  
overseas of agricultural products and  
commodities, and a number of govern­
ment agencies have responsibilities in  
connection with these activities; and
Whereas it is of fundamental im­
portance that we have a national food  
policy directed toward using our agricul­
tural abundance as a national asset to  
meet foreign policy objectives.
NOW , THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me as President of  
the United States, it is ordered as  
follows;
S e c t i o n 1. Executive Order No. 10900  
of January 5, 1961 (26 F.R. 143), headed  
“Administration of the Agricultural  
Trade Development and Assistance Act  
of 1954, as amended,” is hereby amended  
by renumbering sections 6 and 7 thereof  
as sections 7 and 8, respectively, and by  
inserting after section 5 the following  
new section 6:
“ Se c. 6. Director of the Food-for-Peace  
Program.  Subject to the direction of the  
President, the Director of the Food-for-  
Peace Program (provided for in a letter  
of the President bearing the same date  
as this order) shall be responsible for
the continuous supervision and coordi­
nation of the functions hereinabove dele­
gated or otherwise assigned to officers  
or agencies of the Government. The  
foregoing provisions of this section shall  
not be construed as terminating any  
delegation or other assignment of func­
tion made by other sections of this  
order.”
Sec. 2. Executive Order No. 10893 of 
November 8,1960 (25 F.R. 10731) , headed  
“Administration of mutual security and  
related functions,” is hereby amended  
by adding at the end of Part I thereof a  
new section 111, reading as follows;
Sec. 111. Director of the Food-for-  
Peace Program.  Subject to the direction  
of the President, the Director of the  
Food-for-Peace Program shall be re­
sponsible for the continuous supervision  
and coordination of the functions under  
Section 402 of the Act (22 U.S.C. 1922). 
The foregoing provisions of this section  
shall not be construed as superseding  
any delegation or other assignment of  
function made by the Act or by other  
sections of this order.”

ginia, Virginia, North Carolina, South

trict of Columbia and all of the States

Arizona, Nevada, California, Oregon,  
Washington, Alaska, and Hawaii;
(f) “Crude oil” means crude petro­
leum as it is produced at the wellhead;
(g) “Finished products” means any  
one or more of the following petroleum  
oils, or a mixture or combination of such  
oils, which are to be used without fur­
ther processing except blending by  
mechanical means:
(1) Liquefied g a s e s — hydrocarbon  
gases recovered from natural gas or pro­
duced from petroleum refining and kept  
under pressure to maintain a liquid state  
at ambient temperatures;
(2) Gasoline— a refined petroleum  
distillate which by its composition, is  
suitable for use as a carburent in inter­
nal combustion engines;
(3) Jet fuel— a refined petroleum dis­
tillate used to fuel jet propulsion engines;
(4) Naphtha— a refined petroleum  
distillate falling within a distillation  
range overlapping the higher gasoline  
and the lower kerosenes;
(5 ) » Fuel oil— a liquid or liquefiable  
petroleum product burned for lighting or  
for the generation of heat or power and  
derived directly or indirectly from crude  
oil, such as kerosene, range oil, distillate  
fuel oils, gas oil, diesel fuel, topped crude  
oil, residues;
(6) Lubricating oil— a refined petro­
leum distillate or specially treated petro­
leum residue used to lessen friction be­

(7) Residual fuel oil— a topped crude  
oil or viscous residuum which, as ob­
tained in refining or after blending with  
other fuel oil, meets or is the equivalent  
of Military Specification MIL-F-859 for  
Navy Special Fuel Oil and any other

liquefies when heated, in which the pre­
dominating constituents are bitumins,

combination of such oils, which are to be  
further processed other than by blending  
by mechanical means;

partment of the Interior, or his duly

At a session of the Federal Communi­
cations Commission held at its offices in  
Washington, D.C., on the 18th day of  
January 1961;
The Commission has had under con­
sideration the desirability of consolidat­
ing Annual Report Forms O, W ire-tele-  
graph and Ocean-cable Carriers, and R,  
Radiotelegraph Carriers.
The consolidation ordered herein is  
designed to make no change in any re­
porting requirement of substance. The  
separate report form designations, Form  
O, and Form R, are retained but will  
henceforth indicate a single document.  
Certain obsolete schedules or those  
which call for information which ex­
perience has shown the carriers have  
nothing to report on, and are not likely  
to have in the future, have been deleted.
The reporting requirements contained  
in the two annual report forms, Form O  
and Form R, were found to be so similar  
that it seemed a natural step to combine  
them and this similarity made it possible  
to combine many of the schedules in the  
two Forms even to the extent of retain­
ing schedule numbers and titles. There  
are, however, instances of such varia­
tions in the account classifications be­
tween wire-telegraph and ocean-cable,  
on the one hand, and radiotelegraph, on  
the other, that retention of separate re­
porting schedules was found necessary.
The pages of the new combined report  
form are numbered consecutively for  
more ready reference. The size of the  
sheets is the same as in telephone Annual  
Report Form M  prescribed by the Com­
mission and in the Form O  being  
superseded.
Combining of the two report forms  
ordered herein will contribute to. econ­
omy in printing and stocking as com­
pared to the costs of two totally separate  
documents.
A comparative table showing the dis­
position made of the schedules and other  
sheets contained in Forms O  and R  is  
attached to this order .1
It appearing that the consolidation of  
Annual Report Forms O and R  does not  
change in any material respect the re­
porting requirements of the carriers and  
hence that compliance with the public  
notice, procedural, and effective date re­
quirements of section 4 of the Adminis­
trative Procedure Act is unnecessary;  
and
It further appearing that consolida­
tion of the two Forms referred to is  
desirable;

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10916 (26 FR 781, PDF pages 3-8; Federal Register issue of January 26, 1961; govinfo PDF text layer held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10916.txt), headed Executive Order 10916, signed by John F. Kennedy on January 24, 1961. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Inspection of income, estate, and gift tax returns by the Senate Committee on Government Operations). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: the order is one grant, a single sentence opening income, estate and gift tax (years 1947 to 1961, inclusive) returns to inspection by the Senate Committee on Government Operations or any duly authorized subcommittee, followed by a sentence fixing its effective date on filing for publication. The dossier clause starts mid-sentence, so the inventory is corrected (see inventory reason). The grant is limited by its own words to the period of the Eighty-seventh Congress, which I treat as the order's fixed term. The terms of the Members of the Eighty-seventh Congress began at noon on January 3, 1961 and ended at noon on January 3, 1963 (Twentieth Amendment, sections 1 and 2). The Constitution is not among the held texts and no held source states that date, so the end date rests on that constitutional text together with the order's own words; no other source is claimed for it. First end: January 3, 1963 by the order's own terms, recorded inclusive. The exclusive reading (the end when that day begins) is the alternative the owner ruling requires me to disclose, but it fits poorly here because the Congress's terms ran until noon of that day. The three chosen machine searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes plus operative sentences of 17521 saved order texts) each state their coverage with no warning; their coverage notes were read. They search by this order's number, and none returned a hit for it.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The purpose the order states (its studies of Government operations) explains why the committee may inspect and is not a limit on the grant's term; no held text shows that purpose withdrawn or exhausted before the Congress ended. (2) The recital of Treasury Decisions 6132 and 6133 governs how inspection proceeds and sets no end. (3) The effective-date sentence starts the grant and is not an end. (4) The Cruden number lookup in LOOKUPS.md (all held order texts except clause drafts) finds this number only in the held Federal Register text of this order itself and in the held Register page text EO_10915.txt, where it is the printing of this order's own heading on a Register page shared with the neighbouring order. An exact-number search of the held text of EO 12553 (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_12553.txt, the 1986 mass revocation table) finds no entry for this number. No other instrument is shown to have revoked, superseded or terminated the grant before January 3, 1963.","independent_command_check":"The order commands nothing independent of the inspection grant: the Treasury Decisions recital sets the manner of inspection and the effective-date sentence is not a command. No appointment, delegation or direction to an agency survives the grant.","savings_check":"The order has no saving wording. Inspections already made are completed acts that rest on the grant and do not keep it operative after January 3, 1963.","scope_check":"The order has one operative clause and it ends in full on January 3, 1963. The dossier clause was misplaced, so the inventory is corrected as stated in the inventory reason."}

savings_residuals.reason: The order contains no savings, exception or transitional clause; I read its whole text for such wording. Any inspection made while the grant ran is a completed act, and nothing in the order continues the grant after the Eighty-seventh Congress ended. Any later statutory change to the Internal Revenue Code sections the order cites would postdate this end and cannot be a first end.

Executive Order 10915
AMENDING PRIOR EXECUTIVE OR­
DERS TO PROVIDE FOR THE RE­

GRAM
Whereas American agricultural abun­
dance offers a unique opportunity for  
the United States to promote the in­
terests of peace in a significant way and  
to play an important role in helping to  
provide a more adequate diet for peoples  
around the world; and
Whereas exports of farm products are  
of great importance to the domestic  
economy, furnishing approximately 11 
percent of total farm income; and
Whereas many government functions  
and activities relate to the movement  
overseas of agricultural products and  
commodities, and a number of govern­
ment agencies have responsibilities in  
connection with these activities; and
Whereas it is of fundamental im­
portance that we have a national food  
policy directed toward using our agricul­
tural abundance as a national asset to  
meet foreign policy objectives.
NOW , THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me as President of  
the United States, it is ordered as  
follows;
S e c t i o n 1. Executive Order No. 10900  
of January 5, 1961 (26 F.R. 143), headed  
“Administration of the Agricultural  
Trade Development and Assistance Act  
of 1954, as amended,” is hereby amended  
by renumbering sections 6 and 7 thereof  
as sections 7 and 8, respectively, and by  
inserting after section 5 the following  
new section 6:
“ Se c. 6. Director of the Food-for-Peace  
Program.  Subject to the direction of the  
President, the Director of the Food-for-  
Peace Program (provided for in a letter  
of the President bearing the same date  
as this order) shall be responsible for
the continuous supervision and coordi­
nation of the functions hereinabove dele­
gated or otherwise assigned to officers  
or agencies of the Government. The  
foregoing provisions of this section shall  
not be construed as terminating any  
delegation or other assignment of func­
tion made by other sections of this  
order.”
Sec. 2. Executive Order No. 10893 of 
November 8,1960 (25 F.R. 10731) , headed

new section 111, reading as follows;
Sec. 111. Director of the Food-for-

of the President, the Director of the  
Food-for-Peace Program shall be re­
sponsible for the continuous supervision  
and coordination of the functions under  
Section 402 of the Act (22 U.S.C. 1922). 
The foregoing provisions of this section  
shall not be construed as superseding  
any delegation or other assignment of  
function made by the Act or by other  
sections of this order.”

By virtue of the authority vested in me  
by section 55(a) of the Internal Revenue  
Code of 1939 (53 Stat. 29; 26 U.S.C. 55
(a )) and by section 6103(a) of the In ­
ternal Revenue Code of 1954 ( 68A Stat.  
753; 26 U.S.C. 6103(a) ), it is hereby or­
dered that any income, estate, or gift tax  
return for the years 1947 to 1961, inclu­
sive, shall, during the Eighty-seventh  
Congress, be open to inspection by the  
Senate Committee on Government Op­
erations, or by any duly authorized sub­
committee thereof, in connection with  
its studies of the operation of Govern­
ment activities at all levels with a view  
to determining the economy and effi­
ciency of the Government, such inspec­
tion to be in accordance and upon com­
pliance with the rules and regulations  
prescribed by the Secretary of the Treas­
ury in Treasury Decisions 6132 and 6133,  
relating to the inspection of tax returns  
by committees of the Congress, approved  
by the President on May 3, 1955.
This order shall become effective upon  
its filing for publication in the F e d e r a l

At a session of the Federal Communi­
cations Commission held at its offices in  
Washington, D.C., on the 18th day of  
January 1961;
The Commission has had under con­
sideration the desirability of consolidat­
ing Annual Report Forms O, W ire-tele-  
graph and Ocean-cable Carriers, and R,  
Radiotelegraph Carriers.
The consolidation ordered herein is  
designed to make no change in any re­
porting requirement of substance. The  
separate report form designations, Form  
O, and Form R, are retained but will  
henceforth indicate a single document.  
Certain obsolete schedules or those  
which call for information which ex­
perience has shown the carriers have  
nothing to report on, and are not likely  
to have in the future, have been deleted.
The reporting requirements contained  
in the two annual report forms, Form O  
and Form R, were found to be so similar  
that it seemed a natural step to combine  
them and this similarity made it possible  
to combine many of the schedules in the  
two Forms even to the extent of retain­
ing schedule numbers and titles. There  
are, however, instances of such varia­
tions in the account classifications be­
tween wire-telegraph and ocean-cable,  
on the one hand, and radiotelegraph, on  
the other, that retention of separate re­
porting schedules was found necessary.
The pages of the new combined report  
form are numbered consecutively for  
more ready reference. The size of the  
sheets is the same as in telephone Annual  
Report Form M  prescribed by the Com­
mission and in the Form O  being  
superseded.
Combining of the two report forms  
ordered herein will contribute to. econ­
omy in printing and stocking as com­
pared to the costs of two totally separate  
documents.
A comparative table showing the dis­
position made of the schedules and other  
sheets contained in Forms O  and R  is  
attached to this order .1
It appearing that the consolidation of  
Annual Report Forms O and R  does not  
change in any material respect the re­
porting requirements of the carriers and  
hence that compliance with the public  
notice, procedural, and effective date re­
quirements of section 4 of the Adminis­
trative Procedure Act is unnecessary;  
and
It further appearing that consolida­
tion of the two Forms referred to is  
desirable;

Executive Order 10915
AMENDING PRIOR EXECUTIVE OR­
DERS TO PROVIDE FOR THE RE­
SPONSIBILITIES OF THE DIRECTOR  
OF THE FOOD-FOR-PEACE PRO­
GRAM
Whereas American agricultural abun­
dance offers a unique opportunity for  
the United States to promote the in­
terests of peace in a significant way and  
to play an important role in helping to  
provide a more adequate diet for peoples  
around the world; and
Whereas exports of farm products are  
of great importance to the domestic  
economy, furnishing approximately 11 
percent of total farm income; and
Whereas many government functions  
and activities relate to the movement  
overseas of agricultural products and  
commodities, and a number of govern­
ment agencies have responsibilities in  
connection with these activities; and
Whereas it is of fundamental im­
portance that we have a national food  
policy directed toward using our agricul­
tural abundance as a national asset to  
meet foreign policy objectives.
NOW , THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me as President of  
the United States, it is ordered as  
follows;
S e c t i o n 1. Executive Order No. 10900  
of January 5, 1961 (26 F.R. 143), headed  
“Administration of the Agricultural  
Trade Development and Assistance Act  
of 1954, as amended,” is hereby amended  
by renumbering sections 6 and 7 thereof  
as sections 7 and 8, respectively, and by  
inserting after section 5 the following  
new section 6:
“ Se c. 6. Director of the Food-for-Peace  
Program.  Subject to the direction of the  
President, the Director of the Food-for-  
Peace Program (provided for in a letter  
of the President bearing the same date  
as this order) shall be responsible for
the continuous supervision and coordi­
nation of the functions hereinabove dele­
gated or otherwise assigned to officers  
or agencies of the Government. The  
foregoing provisions of this section shall  
not be construed as terminating any  
delegation or other assignment of func­
tion made by other sections of this  
order.”
Sec. 2. Executive Order No. 10893 of 
November 8,1960 (25 F.R. 10731) , headed  
“Administration of mutual security and  
related functions,” is hereby amended  
by adding at the end of Part I thereof a  
new section 111, reading as follows;
Sec. 111. Director of the Food-for-  
Peace Program.  Subject to the direction  
of the President, the Director of the  
Food-for-Peace Program shall be re­
sponsible for the continuous supervision  
and coordination of the functions under  
Section 402 of the Act (22 U.S.C. 1922). 
The foregoing provisions of this section  
shall not be construed as superseding  
any delegation or other assignment of  
function made by the Act or by other  
sections of this order.”

Cargo deadweight tons represent the  
carrying capacity of a tanker, in tons of  
2,240 pounds, less the weight of-fuel,  
water, stores, and other items necessary  
for use on a voyage.
This amendment follows generally the  
proposal published in the F ederal  
R egister  for October 7, 1960 (24 F.R. 
9645). After consideration of the  
numerous comments received on the pro­
posal, several changes have been made;  
among others, changes in the definition  
of “deep-water terminal,” in the require­
ments respecting eligibility for an allo­
cation based on terminal inputs, and in  
the method of computing terminal in­
puts. Allocations of imports of residual  
fuel oil to be used as fuel for District I  
and Districts II-IV  must be made 45 
days before the beginning of the next  
allocation period on April 1, 1961. Ap­
plications for allocations for those Dis­
tricts must be received by February 13, 
1961. Accordingly, it is impracticable to  
give further notice of proposed rule  
making on, or to delay the effective date  
of, this amendment and it shall become  
effective immediately.

Title 4 7 — TELECOMMUNICATION
Chapter I— Federal Communications  
Commission
PART 1—  PRACTICE AND PROCEDURE
PART 43— REPORTS OF COMMUNI­
CATION COMMON CARRIERS AND  
CERTAIN AFFILIATES
Wire-Telegraph a n d  Ocean-Cable  
Carriers, and Radiotelegraph Car­
riers; Annual Report Forms
At a session of the Federal Communi­
cations Commission held at its offices in  
Washington, D.C., on the 18th day of  
January 1961;
The Commission has had under con­
sideration the desirability of consolidat­
ing Annual Report Forms O, W ire-tele-  
graph and Ocean-cable Carriers, and R,  
Radiotelegraph Carriers.
The consolidation ordered herein is  
designed to make no change in any re­
porting requirement of substance. The  
separate report form designations, Form  
O, and Form R, are retained but will  
henceforth indicate a single document.  
Certain obsolete schedules or those  
which call for information which ex­
perience has shown the carriers have  
nothing to report on, and are not likely  
to have in the future, have been deleted.
The reporting requirements contained  
in the two annual report forms, Form O  
and Form R, were found to be so similar  
that it seemed a natural step to combine  
them and this similarity made it possible  
to combine many of the schedules in the  
two Forms even to the extent of retain­
ing schedule numbers and titles. There  
are, however, instances of such varia­
tions in the account classifications be­
tween wire-telegraph and ocean-cable,  
on the one hand, and radiotelegraph, on  
the other, that retention of separate re­
porting schedules was found necessary.
The pages of the new combined report  
form are numbered consecutively for  
more ready reference. The size of the  
sheets is the same as in telephone Annual  
Report Form M  prescribed by the Com­
mission and in the Form O  being  
superseded.
Combining of the two report forms  
ordered herein will contribute to. econ­
omy in printing and stocking as com­
pared to the costs of two totally separate  
documents.
A comparative table showing the dis­
position made of the schedules and other  
sheets contained in Forms O  and R  is  
attached to this order .1
It appearing that the consolidation of  
Annual Report Forms O and R  does not  
change in any material respect the re­
porting requirements of the carriers and  
hence that compliance with the public  
notice, procedural, and effective date re­
quirements of section 4 of the Adminis­
trative Procedure Act is unnecessary;  
and
It further appearing that consolida­
tion of the two Forms referred to is  
desirable;
1  F iled as p a rt o f the origin al docum ent.
It is ordered,  Under authority con­
tained in sections 4(i) and 219  of  
the Communications Act of 1934, as 
amended, that commencing effective for  
the reporting year 1960, a consolidated  
Annual Report Form O and R is adopted  
which follows the general description set  
forth hereinabove and in the attached  
Appendix 1 and a copy of which report  
form is available at the Offices of the  
Commission.
(Sec. 4, 48 Stat. 1066 as amended, 47 U.S.C.  
154. In terprets or applies sec. 219, 48 Stat  
1077, 47 U.S.C. 219)

Title 3— THE PRESIDENT
Executive Order 10935
INSPECTION OF INCOME, EXCESS-  
PROFITS, ESTATE, AND GIFT TAX  
RETURNS BY THE COMMITTEE ON  
UN-AMERICAN ACIVITIES, HOUSE  
OF REPRESENTATIVES
By virtue of the authority vested in me  
by section 55(a) of the Internal Revenue  
Code of 1939, as amended (53 Stat. 29, 54  
Stat. 1008; 26 U.S.C. 55(a) ), and by sec­
tion 6103(a) of the Internal Revenue  
Code of 1954 ( 68A Stat. 753; 26 U.S.C.  
6103(a)), it is hereby ordered that any  
income, excess-profits, estate, or gift tax  
return for the years 1945 to 1961, inclu­
sive, shall, during the Eighty-seventh  
Congress, be open to inspection by the  
Committee on Un-American Activities,  
House of Representatives, or any duly  
authorized subcommittee thereof, for the  
purpose of carrying on those investiga­
tions authorized by clause 18 of Rule XI  
of the Rules of the House of Representa­
tives, agreed to January 3,1961, such in­
spection to be in accordance and upon  
compliance with the rules and regula­
tions prescribed by the Secretary of the  
Treasury in Treasury Decisions 6132 and  
6133, relating to the inspection of returns  
by committees of the Congress, approved  
by the President on May 3, 1955.
This order shall be effective upon its  
filing for publication in the F ederal 
R egister.
John  F. K ennedy
T he White  H ouse ,
April 22,1961.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by its own terms at the end of the Eighty-seventh Congress. Executive Order 10935, signed April 22, 1961 (26 FR 3507, PDF pages 3-3), orders that income, excess-profits, estate and gift tax (years 1945 to 1961, inclusive) returns shall, during the Eighty-seventh Congress, be open to inspection by the Committee on Un-American Activities, House of Representatives, or any duly authorized subcommittee, for the purpose of carrying on the investigations authorized by clause 18 of Rule XI of the Rules of the House of Representatives, agreed to January 3, 1961. The order sets no other term, condition or revocation clause. The terms of the Members of the Eighty-seventh Congress ended at noon on January 3, 1963 under the Twentieth Amendment, so the grant lapsed no later than that day; recorded as 1963-01-03 inclusive, with the exclusive reading (end when that day begins) disclosed as the alternative. The end source is the order's own operative text. No later amending event is held.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by its own terms at the end of the Eighty-seventh Congress. Executive Order 10947, signed June 12, 1961 (26 FR 5283, PDF pages 3-3), orders that income, excess-profits, estate and gift tax (years 1950 to 1961, inclusive) returns shall, during the Eighty-seventh Congress, be open to inspection by the Committee on Public Works, House of Representatives, or any duly authorized subcommittee, in connection with its investigation of the policies, procedures and practices involved in the administration of the Federal-Aid Highway Program, pursuant to House Resolution 23, 87th Congress, agreed to February 6, 1961. The order sets no other term, condition or revocation clause. The terms of the Members of the Eighty-seventh Congress ended at noon on January 3, 1963 under the Twentieth Amendment, so the grant lapsed no later than that day; recorded as 1963-01-03 inclusive, with the exclusive reading (end when that day begins) disclosed as the alternative. The end source is the order's own operative text. No later amending event is held.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10947 (26 FR 5283, PDF pages 3-3; Federal Register issue of June 14, 1961; govinfo PDF text layer held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10947.txt), headed Executive Order 10947, signed by John F. Kennedy on June 12, 1961. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Inspection of income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns by the House Committee on Public Works). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: the order is one grant, a single sentence opening income, excess-profits, estate and gift tax (years 1950 to 1961, inclusive) returns to inspection by the Committee on Public Works, House of Representatives or any duly authorized subcommittee, followed by a sentence fixing its effective date on filing for publication. The dossier clause starts mid-sentence, so the inventory is corrected (see inventory reason). The grant is limited by its own words to the period of the Eighty-seventh Congress, which I treat as the order's fixed term. The terms of the Members of the Eighty-seventh Congress began at noon on January 3, 1961 and ended at noon on January 3, 1963 (Twentieth Amendment, sections 1 and 2). The Constitution is not among the held texts and no held source states that date, so the end date rests on that constitutional text together with the order's own words; no other source is claimed for it. First end: January 3, 1963 by the order's own terms, recorded inclusive. The exclusive reading (the end when that day begins) is the alternative the owner ruling requires me to disclose, but it fits poorly here because the Congress's terms ran until noon of that day. The three chosen machine searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes plus operative sentences of 17521 saved order texts) each state their coverage with no warning; their coverage notes were read. They search by this order's number, and none returned a hit for it.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The purpose the order states (House Resolution 23, 87th Congress) explains why the committee may inspect and is not a limit on the grant's term; no held text shows that purpose withdrawn or exhausted before the Congress ended. (2) The recital of Treasury Decisions 6132 and 6133 governs how inspection proceeds and sets no end. (3) The effective-date sentence starts the grant and is not an end. (4) The Cruden number lookup in LOOKUPS.md (all held order texts except clause drafts) finds this number only in the held Federal Register text of this order itself. An exact-number search of the held text of EO 12553 (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_12553.txt, the 1986 mass revocation table) finds no entry for this number. No other instrument is shown to have revoked, superseded or terminated the grant before January 3, 1963.","independent_command_check":"The order commands nothing independent of the inspection grant: the Treasury Decisions recital sets the manner of inspection and the effective-date sentence is not a command. No appointment, delegation or direction to an agency survives the grant.","savings_check":"The order has no saving wording. Inspections already made are completed acts that rest on the grant and do not keep it operative after January 3, 1963.","scope_check":"The order has one operative clause and it ends in full on January 3, 1963. The dossier clause was misplaced, so the inventory is corrected as stated in the inventory reason."}

savings_residuals.reason: The order contains no savings, exception or transitional clause; I read its whole text for such wording. Any inspection made while the grant ran is a completed act, and nothing in the order continues the grant after the Eighty-seventh Congress ended. Any later statutory change to the Internal Revenue Code sections the order cites would postdate this end and cannot be a first end.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by its own terms at the end of the Eighty-seventh Congress. Executive Order 10966, signed October 10, 1961 (26 FR 9667, PDF pages 3-3), orders that income, excess-profits, estate and gift tax (years 1947 to 1961, inclusive) returns shall, during the Eighty-seventh Congress, be open to inspection by the Committee on Government Operations, House of Representatives, or any duly authorized subcommittee, in connection with its studies of the operation of Government activities at all levels with a view to determining the economy and efficiency of the Government. The order sets no other term, condition or revocation clause. The terms of the Members of the Eighty-seventh Congress ended at noon on January 3, 1963 under the Twentieth Amendment, so the grant lapsed no later than that day; recorded as 1963-01-03 inclusive, with the exclusive reading (end when that day begins) disclosed as the alternative. The end source is the order's own operative text. No later amending event is held.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10966 (26 FR 9667, PDF pages 3-3; Federal Register issue of October 13, 1961; govinfo PDF text layer held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10966.txt), headed Executive Order 10966, signed by John F. Kennedy on October 10, 1961. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Inspection of income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns by the Committee on Government Operations, House of Representatives). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: the order is one grant, a single sentence opening income, excess-profits, estate and gift tax (years 1947 to 1961, inclusive) returns to inspection by the Committee on Government Operations, House of Representatives or any duly authorized subcommittee, followed by a sentence fixing its effective date on filing for publication. The grant is limited by its own words to the period of the Eighty-seventh Congress, which I treat as the order's fixed term. The terms of the Members of the Eighty-seventh Congress began at noon on January 3, 1961 and ended at noon on January 3, 1963 (Twentieth Amendment, sections 1 and 2). The Constitution is not among the held texts and no held source states that date, so the end date rests on that constitutional text together with the order's own words; no other source is claimed for it. First end: January 3, 1963 by the order's own terms, recorded inclusive. The exclusive reading (the end when that day begins) is the alternative the owner ruling requires me to disclose, but it fits poorly here because the Congress's terms ran until noon of that day. The three chosen machine searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes plus operative sentences of 17521 saved order texts) each state their coverage with no warning; their coverage notes were read. They search by this order's number, and none returned a hit for it.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The purpose the order states (its studies of Government operations) explains why the committee may inspect and is not a limit on the grant's term; no held text shows that purpose withdrawn or exhausted before the Congress ended. (2) The recital of Treasury Decisions 6132 and 6133 governs how inspection proceeds and sets no end. (3) The effective-date sentence starts the grant and is not an end. (4) The Cruden number lookup in LOOKUPS.md (all held order texts except clause drafts) finds this number only in the held Federal Register text of this order itself and in the held Register page texts EO_10967.txt, EO_10968.txt, EO_10969.txt, where it is the printing of this order's own heading on a Register page shared with the neighbouring order. An exact-number search of the held text of EO 12553 (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_12553.txt, the 1986 mass revocation table) finds no entry for this number. No other instrument is shown to have revoked, superseded or terminated the grant before January 3, 1963.","independent_command_check":"The order commands nothing independent of the inspection grant: the Treasury Decisions recital sets the manner of inspection and the effective-date sentence is not a command. No appointment, delegation or direction to an agency survives the grant.","savings_check":"The order has no saving wording. Inspections already made are completed acts that rest on the grant and do not keep it operative after January 3, 1963.","scope_check":"The order has one operative clause and it ends in full on January 3, 1963. The dossier inventory (one whole-order clause) is complete."}

savings_residuals.reason: The order contains no savings, exception or transitional clause; I read its whole text for such wording. Any inspection made while the grant ran is a completed act, and nothing in the order continues the grant after the Eighty-seventh Congress ended. Any later statutory change to the Internal Revenue Code sections the order cites would postdate this end and cannot be a first end.

may deem appropriate for the civil ad­

this order shall continue in force until

administration of Palmyra Island or un­

specify.

myra Island” means the place of that 
name, consisting of a group of islets lo­
cated in the Pacific Ocean approximately

torial waters of that place and includes 
also the reefs surrounding that place or 
any part thereof.

Executive order or proclamation is in­
consistent with the provisions of this

modify the authority or responsibility of

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10981 (26 FR 12749, PDF pages 3-3; Federal Register issue of December 30, 1961; govinfo PDF text layer held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10981.txt), headed Executive Order 10981, signed by John F. Kennedy on December 28, 1961. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Inspection of income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns by the Senate Committee on the Judiciary). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: the order is one grant, a single sentence opening income, excess-profits, estate and gift tax (years 1950 to 1961, inclusive) returns to inspection by the Senate Committee on the Judiciary or any duly authorized subcommittee, followed by a sentence fixing its effective date on filing for publication. The grant is limited by its own words to the period of the Eighty-seventh Congress, which I treat as the order's fixed term. The terms of the Members of the Eighty-seventh Congress began at noon on January 3, 1961 and ended at noon on January 3, 1963 (Twentieth Amendment, sections 1 and 2). The Constitution is not among the held texts and no held source states that date, so the end date rests on that constitutional text together with the order's own words; no other source is claimed for it. First end: January 3, 1963 by the order's own terms, recorded inclusive. The exclusive reading (the end when that day begins) is the alternative the owner ruling requires me to disclose, but it fits poorly here because the Congress's terms ran until noon of that day. The three chosen machine searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes plus operative sentences of 17521 saved order texts) each state their coverage with no warning; their coverage notes were read. They search by this order's number, and none returned a hit for it.

(2) The recital of Treasury Decisions 6132 and 6133 governs how inspection proceeds and sets no end. (3) The effective-date sentence starts the grant and is not an end. (4) The Cruden number lookup in LOOKUPS.md (all held order texts except clause drafts) finds this number only in the held Federal Register text of this order itself. An exact-number search of the held text of EO 12553 (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_12553.txt, the 1986 mass revocation table) finds no entry for this number. No other instrument is shown to have revoked, superseded or terminated the grant before January 3, 1963.","independent_command_check":"The order commands nothing independent of the inspection grant: the Treasury Decisions recital sets the manner of inspection and the effective-date sentence is not a command. No appointment, delegation or direction to an agency survives the grant.","savings_check":"The order has no saving wording. By virtue of the authority vested in me by section 55(a) of the 
Internal* Revenue Code of 1939, as amended (53 Stat. 29; 54 Stat. 
1008; 26 U.S.C. (1952 Ed.) 55(a)), ‘ and by section 6103(a) of the

under section 101 or 165(a) of the 1939 Code, as amended (53 Stat.

business, pursuant to House Resolution 46, 87th Congress, agreed to 
February 6, 1961, such inspection to be in accordance and upon com­
pliance with the rules and regulations prescribed by the Secretary of 
the Treasury in Treasury Decisions 6132 and 6133, relating to the 
inspection of returns by committees of the Congress, approved by the 
President on May 3, 1955.

in the F ederal R egister.
